name: antipodal_sign_fibre
statement: A sign fibre is a nonempty set A \subseteq {\pm 1}^r with A = -A (antipodal), usually assumed spanning (spans R^r) and full closed.
notes: Central deterministic object of Layer II.

name: entropy_defect_ell
statement: For X uniform on a sign fibre A \subseteq {\pm 1}^r: H(X) = log_2 |A|, and the entropy defect is \ell(A) := r - H(X) = r - log_2 |A|, the number of bits lost relative to the full cube.
notes: In the random-matrix application, \ell is the entropy budget available to pay for algebraic coincidences; converting it into residual directions is the packet's main difficulty (p.5). | MERGED (sources_S1-S5.jsonl digest, kept the synthesis statement as fuller); displaced variant preserved: For a spanning antipodal sign fibre $A\subseteq\{\pm1\}^r$, the entropy defect is $\ell(A)=r-\log_2|A|$. | source-digest notes: Real-valued, not integer. Used throughout S1 as the entropy budget that all batching charges must fit inside.

name: sign_form_fibre_S
statement: General bridge formulation: given sign-valued linear forms h_a, set S = {x in {\pm 1}^r : h_a . x in {\pm 1} for every a}, with |S| = 2^{r-\ell} defining \ell. Rows already equal to signed coordinates are harmless and may be discarded before constructing the two-shadow graph.
notes: The 'two-shadow graph' is referenced but not defined within pp.1-18 (defined in later dossier pages).

name: full_dual
statement: For a sign fibre A spanning a real vector space, the full dual D(A) is the collection of linear forms taking only the values \pm 1 on A, considered projectively up to sign. A displayed coordinate family is coordinate-full when it exhausts this projective full dual.

name: closure_full_closed
statement: cl(A) = {y in {\pm 1}^r : g(y) in {\pm 1} for every g in D(A)}; the fibre is full closed when A = cl(A). Closure is intrinsic.
notes: Purpose: prevents an argument from silently ignoring extra sign points compatible with every available equation.

name: coordinate_basis
statement: A coordinate basis is a linear basis drawn from the full dual D(A). The selector distance d_cb optimizes over residual spaces AND over these bases; selected dense witness rows can sometimes replace coordinate directions.
notes: Dossier's recorded danger: basis exchange does NOT imply that all unselected rows become cheap.

name: geometric_distance_dgeo
statement: Let F = {f_i} be the projective coordinate forms on a fibre. A geometric residual space is R = span{f_i - sigma f_j : sigma in {\pm 1}}; k_F(R) is the number of signed projective classes of the f_i modulo R (all forms in R form a single zero class). d_geo = the minimum residual dimension that leaves no more classes than the ambient rank permits.

name: selector_distance_dcb
statement: Choose a coordinate basis from the full dual and assign every full-dual form to a signed basis representative; the residuals of all assignments must lie in a common space R. d_cb(A) = min dim R, minimized over both the basis and the selectors.
notes: Stronger than d_geo; the explicit basis selectors are what the centered-moment encoding needs (p.7).

name: conditional_defect_LQW
statement: A nonroot block carries incoming boundary signs W and private signs Q = (Q_1, ..., Q_q). The conditional entropy loss is L_{Q|W} = q - H(Q | W). Boundary-only forms are assigned to the parent; conditional defects then telescope down the recursive block tree.
notes: Telescoping is why a uniform rooted theorem would globalize with one absolute constant (p.8).

name: connector_absorption
statement: Ancestors may already have paid a residual subspace R_< \subseteq span W. Connector absorption is the requirement R \cap span W \subseteq R_<: any pure boundary residual created by the child must already have been paid by the parent.
notes: Not bookkeeping decoration: without it the same boundary direction can be charged at each generation, a depth loss even when every local quotient bound is linear (p.8).

name: affine_state_sets_B0_B2_M
statement: B_0 = {eta in {\pm 1}^{12} : sum_i eta_i = 0}, B_2 = {eta : sum_i eta_i = 2}; |B_0| = 924, |B_2| = 792. M = the three one-minority states of three signs.

name: exceptional_sets_Omega0_Omega1
statement: Omega_0 = B_0 x M and Omega_1 = (B_0 x {xi(1), xi(2)}) \cup (B_2 x {xi(3)}), where xi(1), xi(2), xi(3) are the one-minority states forming M.

name: shared_h_homogenization_setup
statement: C = (c_1, ..., c_m) in R^{3 x m}, S_t = {x in {\pm 1}^m : Cx = t}, W = ker C, old coordinate forms f_i = x_i|_W. Homogenize: C-hat = [C | -t], W-hat = ker C-hat, h = the last coordinate form. Antipodal homogenized fibre A-hat_t = {(x,1) : x in S_t} \cup {(-x,-1) : x in S_t} = W-hat \cap {\pm 1}^{m+1}. Row rank three gives dim W-hat = m-2 = dim W + 1.
notes: Extraction glyphs 'bC', 'cW', 'bAt' are hats (C-hat, W-hat, A-hat). Delicate issue: descending a low-dimensional residual plane from W-hat to the affine fibre - the homogenizer can share a quotient class with an old form, and restriction to h = 0 may create or remove mergers; the shared-h analysis classifies the only saturated pattern in which the homogeneous corank-three theorem does not immediately descend.

name: entropy-sharpened-residual-rank-theorem
statement: For every realized core pattern the entire vector X_N0 is deterministic, so H(XC, X_N0) = H(XC); entropy then gives |N0| ≤ ell. Selecting the signed coordinate lambda_a*xj for each conditionally free private coordinate leaves all residuals in the coordinate span of C ∪ N0, proving d(H) ≤ 9*4^ell + ell and consequently dcb(A) ≤ 9*4^(ell(A)) + ell(A) for every spanning full-closed antipodal sign fibre (over R and the odd finite fields of the compression theorem). The quantifier 'never free for EVERY realized core pattern' is essential; weaker coordinatewise conditioning would not justify the entropy identity.

name: intrinsic-cube-model
statement: Assume the affine fibre spans its expected affine flat and the homogenized displayed coordinates are projectively simple and coordinate-full. Choose a basis g1,...,gR of the full dual of the homogenized antipodal fibre A_hat_t (R = m-2) and define Phi: W_hat -> R^R by Phi(w) = (g1(w),...,gR(w)). Spanning makes Phi an isomorphism; each gi is sign-valued on the fibre, so Phi(A_hat_t) lies in the intrinsic cube {±1}^R and is antipodal. Coordinate-fullness gives closure: any cube point satisfying every intrinsic full-dual equation pulls back into W_hat ∩ {±1}^(m+1) = A_hat_t. The intrinsic image is full closed with exactly R+3 projective full-dual forms (the m+1 = R+3 displayed coordinates).

name: connector_absorption_criterion
statement: Write chosen residual generators uniquely as r_a = b_a + p_a, with b_a in B = span W and p_a in P = span Q. Then R intersect B is contained in R_< IFF ker P0 is contained in ker Bbar IFF Bbar = T o P0 for some linear map T. For network-type residual matrices it suffices to test the kernel inclusion on a fundamental-cycle basis: every pure boundary dependency exposed by private cancellation must be an ancestor-paid cycle sum.

Then: T nonconstant on Omega_0 implies N_s(T; Omega_0) <= 4788, and T nonconstant on Omega_1 implies N_s(T; Omega_1) <= 4776. Uniform in both T and s. Unequal-coefficient case: conditioning on the other ten signs gives at most C(10,5)*3 + 2*C(10,6)*2 = 756 + 840 = 1596 weighted completions per upper minority state, and 3*1596 = 4788; equal coefficients: nonidentical translates of the (1,2,1) kernel give the smaller 4776 bound for Omega_1.

Subtracting that combination leaves a nonzero old row supported only on the lower equal pair - a support-two relation forbidden in the projectively simple configuration. So every case gives either the 4788/4776 counting loss or an immediate structural contradiction.

name: two-shadow-graph-and-weighted-batching
statement: For sign-valued rows ha on S = {x ∈ {±1}^r : ha.x ∈ {±1} for every a} (signed-coordinate rows discarded), let Ea = supp(ha). The two-shadow graph Gamma on [r] has an edge ij whenever some Ea contains both i and j. Batching data: fix a maximum matching P1,...,PN of Gamma; greedily choose a remaining pair, select a witness support Es containing it, and remove the batch Bs of all remaining matching pairs meeting Es; set as = |Bs|, Vs = union of the pairs in Bs, Us = Es ∩ Vs.

name: weighted-batching-lemma
statement: In the greedy weighted batching: |Us| ≥ as + 1 for every batch, the sets Us are pairwise disjoint, and an earlier witness support is disjoint from every later Ut. The batching is weighted: a witness meeting many disjoint matching pairs is charged by its full Littlewood-Offord atom loss rather than by a single 3/4 factor multiplied by its support size. This is the step that improves the old common-core size O((1+ell)*4^ell) to O(4^ell).

name: reverse-triangular-exposure
statement: Condition on all signs outside the union of the Us and expose the disjoint blocks in reverse order Uk, Uk-1, ..., U1. When Us is peeled, every earlier selected-row indicator is independent of the variables being exposed (earlier witness supports avoid later U-sets), and variables in earlier Ut remain arbitrary parameters in the target. This yields Pr(hs.X ∈ {±1} | previous exposure) ≤ psi(as+1), and multiplying in reverse order gives 2^(-ell) ≤ prod_s psi(as+1). Audit repair: one must use Us, not all of Es; if |Us| > as+1, first condition on the extra active coordinates, then apply the (as+1)-term atom bound. With that repair the argument is rigorous over R and the specified finite fields.

name: two-point-atom-bound
statement: Target-uniform two-point atom bound: with u active variables (all coefficients nonzero), the probability of hitting either of two prescribed targets is at most psi(u) = min(3/4, 2^(1-u)*binom(u, floor(u/2))) ≤ min(3/4, 2/sqrt(u)). For u = 2 the 3/4 estimate is the nondegenerate parallelogram bound; for u ≥ 3 it is twice the central-binomial one-point mass. Over Fp the correct statement is NOT merely 'no wrap': invoke the finite-group one-point Littlewood-Offord theorem when u < p and all active coefficients are nonzero, then take a union bound over the two targets.

name: weighted-compression-arithmetic
statement: From the atom bound, as + 1 ≤ 4*4^(cs). With C* = sum_s cs and 4^beta = 16/9, a convexity calculation gives (sum_s 4^(cs))/4^(C*) ≤ m*(16/9)^(-(m-1)) ≤ 9/8, where m is the number of nonempty batches (the trivial N = 0 case is separated first). Therefore N = sum_s as ≤ 4*sum_s 4^(cs) ≤ (9/2)*4^ell. The endpoints of a maximum matching form a vertex cover C of Gamma, so |C| ≤ 2N ≤ 9*4^ell. No two-shadow edge survives outside a vertex cover, hence every row support contains at most one coordinate outside C.
notes: Constant 9 explicitly not claimed sharp; the structural gain is paying dense rows their full atom loss, eliminating the old 1+ell factor. Arithmetic independently re-derived here: max over m ≥ 1 of m*(9/16)^(m-1) is 9/8 at m = 2 - checks. Superscripts flattened in extraction ('9 4ℓ' = 9*4^ell).

name: weighted-two-shadow-compression-theorem
statement: Let K = R, or K = Fp with odd p > r. Suppose S = {x ∈ {±1}^r : ha.x ∈ {±1} for every a} with |S| = 2^(r-ell). After discarding signed-coordinate rows, there is a set C ⊆ [r] with |C| ≤ 9*4^ell such that |supp(ha) setminus C| ≤ 1 for every a: every sign-valued row is a core form plus at most one private coordinate (a star over one common core). This is an unconditional high-corank theorem, applying independently of any low-corank decomposition. Explicit limitation: the core is exponential in ell, so this result alone cannot yield the desired uniform LINEAR entropy-rigidity estimate.
notes: Independent audit passed after six precise repairs (p.37). Creates the star-over-core form needed by the entropy-sharpened residual argument and enlarges the controlled endpoint range.

name: conditionally-free-coordinate-and-N0
statement: Given the common core C, every row can be written ha(x) = qa(xC) + lambda_a*xj with at most one j ∉ C. Coordinate j is CONDITIONALLY FREE if both signs of Xj occur above some realized core value XC = c; evaluating the row at the two points forces qa(c) = 0 and lambda_a = ±1. N0 := the set of outside coordinates that are never conditionally free, i.e. not free above any realized core pattern.

name: conditional-exponential-cyclic-block-theorem

It yields selectors whose new residual rank modulo the boundary obeys dim((R + span W)/span W) ≤ 9*4^(L(Q|W)) + L(Q|W). This is a genuine affine, target-uniform theorem: the selected rows may have boundary-dependent targets, and the Littlewood-Offord bounds are uniform in those targets. It does NOT prove connector absorption: quotient rank is controlled after modding out the whole boundary span, but a residual combination could still produce a new pure boundary direction.

Without absorption the same boundary direction can be charged again at each generation of the recursive block tree, producing a depth loss even when every local quotient bound is linear or exponential.

All selected dense witnesses can be inserted simultaneously after O(ell) exchanges. If an old selector used a removed pivot Q_{p_s}, select the witness Y_s and add the discrepancy e_s = Q_{p_s} - Y_s: at most one new direction per exchange. Under bounded congestion the exchanged-basis quotient rank remains linear.

name: rooted_NAE_cycle_family
statement: For n >= 4: A_n = {(a, b_1,...,b_n) in {+-1}^{n+1} : a + b_i + b_{i+1} in {+-1} for all i, indices cyclic}. On the half a=1 the set {i : b_i = 1} is an independent set of the cycle C_n; the a=-1 half is antipodal. Hence |A_n| = 2*L_n (L_n the n-th Lucas number) and ell(A_n) = n - log2 L_n. The fibre is full closed and its projective full dual is exactly D_n = {A, B_i, C_i : i in Z/nZ} with A = e_0, B_i = e_i, C_i = e_0 + e_i + e_{i+1}. The full-dual real matroid is three-connected.
notes: Header: AUDITED EXACT FAMILY. Genuine high-corank cyclic test case; three-connectivity makes it a probe of strategies relying only on coarse matroid connectivity.

name: binary_quotient_count_lower_bound
statement: Let S_n = {0} union {u_i} union {u_i + u_{i+1}} in F_2^n (indices cyclic; |S_n| = 2n+1, u_i the coordinate vectors). For every w-dimensional subspace W of F_2^n: |S_n/W| >= 2n + 1 - 3w. Proof: choose n-w coordinate images forming a quotient basis; removing the other w cycle vertices destroys at most 2w edges, so at least n-2w distinct weight-two basis sums remain, in addition to zero and the n-w singleton images.
notes: Purely binary counting statement; feeds the geometric-distance lower bound via the mod-2 transfer.

name: real_residual_mod2_transfer
statement: To transfer a real signed residual space R (dim d) to the binary quotient: span only the integral witnesses of its actual signed class equalities and the zero class, obtaining a rational subspace R_0 inside R of dimension d_0 <= d. Its saturated integer lattice is primitive, so reduction modulo 2 preserves dimension d_0 and can only merge classes. Translating the full dual D_n by A identifies it (mod 2) with S_n. Hence a feasible real quotient with at most n+1 classes forces d >= ceil(n/3).
notes: Flattened 'd >= ln 3 m' = ceil(n/3). The rationalization step was explicitly re-checked by the audit (p.46).

name: cycle_geometric_distance_exact
statement: dgeo(A_n) = ceil(n/3) for the rooted NAE cycle family. Lower bound: binary quotient lemma + mod-2 transfer. Upper bound: choose an independent set U in V(C_n) with |U| = ceil(n/3) and quotient by the independent residuals A + B_u, u in U; the remaining signed classes are represented by the components and cliques of C_n - U, at most 1 + (n-|U|) + (n-2|U|) = 2n+1-3|U| <= n+1 classes.
notes: Audit verified: rationalization step, the zero class, all residue classes of n mod 3, endpoint cases of the real-matroid connectivity proof, and that every displayed dual column is a nonloop and noncoloop (closing singleton separation cases).

name: cycle_optimal_selector_basis
statement: Choose an independent dominating set U in C_n of size d = ceil(n/3) whose cyclic gaps have (edge-)length two or three. Put L_u = A + B_u and R = span{L_u : u in U}; the L_u are independent. Orient the cycle: in a length-two gap u-v-u' take basis forms B_v, C_v; in a length-three gap u-v-w-u' take B_v, C_v, C_w. Together with A these are exactly n+1 full-dual forms, linearly independent by backward substitution through each gap. Modulo R: B_u = -A, C_u = B_v, B_w = C_w in the relevant gap cases, so every full-dual form has a signed basis representative with residual in R. Hence dcb(A_n) = dgeo(A_n) = ceil(n/3).
notes: Explicit optimal certificate, not just an existence bound. Form count checks: sum of gap lengths = n edges, so d gaps contribute n forms, plus A = n+1.

name: cycle_activation_cell_inequality
statement: For u in U let Z_u record whether the residual L_u = A + B_u is active. For every activation pattern z in {0,1}^U, the optimal selector certificate satisfies |(A_n)_z| <= 2^{n+1-d-|z|}, d = ceil(n/3). Proof: on the a=1 half, z records the intersection of an independent set of C_n with U; a length-two gap has 2,1,1 completions and a length-three gap 3,2,1, according to the sum s+t of its endpoint states, both bounded by 2^{g-1-(s+t)/2} (g = gap edge-length). Multiplying over gaps gives 2^{n-d-|z|} completions; antipodality supplies the factor two. Summing the cells: |A_n|/2^{n+1} <= (3/4)^d, i.e. d <= ell(A_n)/log2(4/3).
notes: Solves the cycle in the stronger CELLWISE form needed for recursive entropy charging, not merely a class-count quotient. Exponents 2^{n+1-d-|z|}, 2^{g-1-(s+t)/2}, (3/4)^d reconstructed from flattened extraction; arithmetic re-verified (sum of (g-1) over gaps = n-d, sum of endpoint states = 2|z|).

name: cycle_connector_transversality
statement: Treat the root sign A as the incoming boundary and the B_i as private coordinates. The optimal residuals L_u = A + B_u project to the DISTINCT private coordinates B_u, hence are independent modulo the boundary, and no nontrivial combination becomes a pure boundary form: R intersect span{A} = 0. The optimal cycle certificate is therefore connector-transverse with zero boundary surcharge and satisfies the common-lift criterion automatically.
notes: Strategic reading (dossier's words): rooted NAE cycles are dense enough to refute the constant-one ceiling lemma yet coherent enough to admit the exact rooted certificate; high corank and three-connectivity are not the obstruction - connector incoherence is.

name: d_cb_signed_selector_residual_rank

notes: Always $d_{\rm geo}\le d_{\rm cb}$. Equality holds for the rooted-NAE cycle family at high corank (see rooted_nae_cycle_exact_dcb).

name: d_geo_signed_projective_class_distance
statement: With $C\in\mathbb R^{3\times m}$ of rank 3, $S_t=\{x\in\{\pm1\}^m:Cx=t\}$, $W=\ker C$, $r=\dim W=m-3$, $f_i=x_i|_W\in W^*$: a geometric residual is $R=\operatorname{span}\{f_i-\sigma f_j:\sigma\in\{\pm1\}\}\le W^*$; $k_F(R)$ counts signed projective classes of the $f_i$ modulo $R$ (all forms lying in $R$ count as one zero class); $d_{\rm geo}(F)=\min\{\dim R:k_F(R)\le r\}$. Tag (1) of S5.

name: two_shadow_graph_Gamma
statement: Let $h_a\in\mathbb R^r$ and $S=\{x\in\{\pm1\}^r:h_a\cdot x\in\{\pm1\}\ \forall a\}$, $|S|=2^{r-\ell}$ (tag 12). Delete rows already equal to signed coordinates, put $E_a=\operatorname{supp}h_a$. The two-shadow graph $\Gamma$ on $[r]$ has $ij\in E(\Gamma)$ when some $E_a$ contains both $i$ and $j$.
notes: The row deletion step is essential: rows already equal to signed coordinates carry no two-shadow.

name: weighted_two_shadow_compression_thm_5_1
statement: There is a vertex cover $C\subseteq[r]$ of $\Gamma$ with $\boxed{|C|\le 9\cdot4^{\ell}}$ (tag 13) such that every $E_a$ contains at most one coordinate outside $C$.
source: dossier p.60 (S1 lines 261-266); proof pp.60-62 (S1 lines 273-320)
notes: $|C|=2N$ where $N$ is the size of a maximum matching in $\Gamma$; $N\le(9/2)4^\ell$. The endpoints of a maximum matching form a vertex cover, which is what gives the 'at most one coordinate outside $C$' property.

name: greedy_batching_peel_method
statement: Take a maximum matching $P_1,\dots,P_N$ in $\Gamma$. Greedily choose a remaining pair, a witness row $E_s$ containing it, and remove the batch $B_s$ of all remaining matching pairs meeting $E_s$; put $a_s=|B_s|$. Batches partition the matching. With $V_s$ the endpoints of $B_s$ and $U_s=E_s\cap V_s$: $|U_s|\ge a_s+1$ (tag 14), the $U_s$ are disjoint, and $E_s$ avoids every later $U_t$. Condition outside $\bigcup_s U_s$ and peel $U_k,\dots,U_1$ in reverse exposure order.
notes: Key independence bookkeeping: earlier selected row indicators are independent of the set being peeled, and variables in earlier $U_t$'s are held as arbitrary parameters. This is exactly why the Littlewood-Offord input must be TARGET-UNIFORM (two-point form).

name: psi_batching_charge_inequalities
statement: $2^{-\ell}\le\prod_s\psi(a_s+1)$ (tag 15) where $\psi(u)=\min\{3/4,\,2^{1-u}\binom{u}{\lfloor u/2\rfloor}\}\le\min\{3/4,\,2/\sqrt u\}$ (tag 16). With $c_s=-\log_2\psi(a_s+1)$ and $\beta=\log_2(4/3)$: $c_s\ge\beta$, $\sum_s c_s\le\ell$, $a_s+1\le4\cdot4^{c_s}$ (tag 17). Since $4^\beta=16/9$, $\sum_s4^{c_s}\le\frac98 4^{\sum_s c_s}\le\frac98 4^{\ell}$ (tag 18).
notes: VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY (this campaign, 2026-08-19, exact arithmetic): $4^{\log_2(4/3)}=(4/3)^2=16/9$; $a_s+1\le4\cdot4^{c_s}$ follows from $\psi\le2/\sqrt u$; and the constant $9/8$ in (18) is EXACTLY the worst case $N=2$ of $\sum x_s/\prod x_s$ over $x_s\ge16/9$ (N=1 gives 1, N=2 gives 1.125, N=3 gives 0.949). Also $c_s\ge\max\{\beta,\tfrac12\log_2(a_s+1)-1\}$ (S1 line 507).

name: entropy_sharpened_residual_rank_thm_5_2
statement: If $S$ is nonempty and antipodal then, for the fixed input basis, $\boxed{d(H)\le 9\cdot4^{\ell}+\ell}$ (tag 19). Proof: every row is $h_a(x)=q_a(x_C)+\lambda_a x_j$ for at most one $j\notin C$ (tag 20); if $j$ is conditionally free (both signs of $X_j$ occur above some realized core value $X_C=c$) then $q_a(c)=0$ and $\lambda_a=\pm1$ (tag 21), so selecting $\lambda_a x_j$ leaves a core-supported residual. If $N_0$ is the never-free outside set, $X_{N_0}$ is a deterministic function of $X_C$, giving $|N_0|\le\ell-(|C|-H(X_C))\le\ell$ (tag 22).
notes: All residuals lie in the coordinate span of $C\cup N_0$, hence dimension $\le|C|+|N_0|\le9\cdot4^\ell+\ell$. The entropy step uses $r-\ell=H(X)\le H(X_C)+r-|C|-|N_0|$ for uniform $X\in S$. The free/never-free dichotomy is the reusable part.

statement: If $W$ is a sign boundary and $Q$ a private sign basis of size $q$, the conditional entropy defect is $L_{Q\mid W}=q-H(Q\mid W)$. Tag (23).
notes: Real-valued and can be arbitrarily small (see one_private_vertex_interval_no_defect_only_bound). $H$ is in bits; $Q$ conditioned on the boundary variables.

name: conditional_exponential_quotient_bound_24
statement: The same target-uniform proof yields selectors whose new residual rank modulo the boundary is $\boxed{\dim\frac{R+\operatorname{span}W}{\operatorname{span}W}\le 9\cdot4^{L_{Q\mid W}}+L_{Q\mid W}}$. Tag (24).

name: kappa_entropy_normalized_congestion
statement: $\kappa=\max_s\dfrac{a_s}{c_s}$ with $c_s=-\log_2\psi(a_s+1)$. Tag (24a).
notes: Entropy-NORMALIZED congestion: a batch is cheap not when it is small but when its size is proportional to the entropy it consumes. $\kappa$ is basis- and batching-dependent, which is why the residual class is defined by 'in every useful basis'.

name: bounded_congestion_linear_rigidity_thm_5_3
statement: For the conditional block of (23), $\sum_s c_s\le L_{Q\mid W}$ and $N=\sum_s a_s\le\kappa L_{Q\mid W}$ (tag 24b); the matching endpoints give a private core of size $\le2\kappa L_{Q\mid W}$, and the free/never-free entropy step adds $\le L_{Q\mid W}$ further private directions, whence $\boxed{\dim\frac{R+\operatorname{span}W}{\operatorname{span}W}\le(2\kappa+1)L_{Q\mid W}}$. Tag (24c)/(2a).
notes: Independently audited PASS per the S1 ledger. This is a QUOTIENT-rank bound only; it carries no absorption clause. Corollary: if every selected witness has private support $\le s$ then $\kappa\le(s-1)/\beta$, giving the absolute coefficient $1+2(s-1)/\beta$; so every bounded-support homogeneous high-corank block satisfies genuine linear rigidity. Exchanging selected witnesses into the coordinate basis costs a further $L_{Q\mid W}/\beta$ (S1 lines 416-421).

Then $\boxed{R\cap\operatorname{span}W\subseteq R_<\iff\ker P\subseteq\ker\overline B\iff\overline B=T\circ P\text{ for some linear }T}$. Tag (24e).
notes: EXACT algebraic certificate for the missing absorption clause; this is the 'common linear lift' condition. Any displayed kernel basis is a finite certificate. S1 line 443: bounded congestion PLUS paid cycle sums is a complete connector-ready linear theorem.

name: endpoint_encoding_exponent_25
statement: For a rank-$r$, size-$k$ component, the existing ternary basis-mass encoding has exponent $-(n-r)\ell+O\bigl(d_{\rm cb}k+(k-r)\log r+r+n\bigr)$. Tag (25).
notes: This is the Layer-II/Layer-III interface: only $d_{\rm cb}$ enters, multiplied by $k$. Everything the deterministic rigidity programme buys enters the endpoint through this one term.

name: endpoint_gain_from_exponential_bridge
statement: With (19), every component sequence with $k=O(n/\log n)$, $\ell\to\infty$, and $4^{\ell}=o(\ell\log n)$ (tag 26) has the required exponential saving. Hence any sequence not covered by (26) has a subsequence on which $4^\ell\gtrsim\ell\log n$, and there, up to constants, $\ell\ge\tfrac12\log_2\log n+\tfrac12\log_2\log\log n-O(1)$ (tag 27).
notes: Fixed $\ell$ was already handled by the fixed-core enumeration. This improves the previous $O((1+\ell)4^\ell)$ common-core range but does NOT cover all admissible $\ell$. Verified: $4^\ell\gtrsim\ell\log n$ gives $2\ell\ge\log_2\log n+\log_2\ell$, consistent with (27).

name: endpoint_gain_from_bounded_congestion
statement: In the same range $k=O(n/\log n)$ one has $n-r=(1-o(1))n$, while (24c) contributes $O(\kappa\ell k)=O\!\left(\frac{\kappa}{\log n}n\ell\right)$ to the encoding exponent (tag 27a). Hence every homogeneous component sequence admitting a batching with $\kappa=o(\log n)$ (tag 27b) also has the required saving.
notes: Orthogonal to (26). Fixed-defect cases handled separately. This is the arithmetic behind the campaign's transfer-lane observation that any UNIFORM coefficient $o(\log n)$ suffices at the endpoint interface -- an absolute constant is strictly more than the moment bookkeeping consumes.

name: residual_obstruction_is_polylog_dense
statement: An unresolved nonsummable sequence must simultaneously lie beyond (26) and have $\kappa\gtrsim\log n$ in every useful basis. Since $c_s\ge\max\{\beta,\tfrac12\log_2(a_s+1)-1\}$, such a batching contains a witness meeting $\Omega(\log n\log\log n)$ disjoint matching pairs; the surviving core therefore has genuinely polylogarithmically dense rows, not merely unbounded support.
notes: This is the sharpest available characterization of the residual class in pp.55-112: 'a substantially denser obstruction than arbitrary high corank'. Both conditions are required simultaneously.

name: simultaneous_witness_basis_exchange_28
statement: Let $E_1,\dots,E_k$ be the selected witness rows in deletion order; from each witness pair choose one pivot $p_s\in E_s$. The pivots are distinct and $E_s$ contains no later pivot $p_t$ ($t>s$), so $(h_s(p_t))_{s,t=1}^k$ is triangular with nonzero diagonal. Hence $\boxed{\{h_1,\dots,h_k\}\cup\{e_i:i\notin\{p_1,\dots,p_k\}\}\text{ is a coordinate basis}}$ (tag 28), and $k\le\ell/\log_2(4/3)$ (tag 29).
notes: All selected dense witnesses can be inserted simultaneously after only $O(\ell)$ basis exchanges. $1/\log_2(4/3)=2.4094208\ldots$ appears here as an UPPER-bound coefficient on the witness count -- do NOT conflate it with the S6 (p.113) LOWER floor $C\ge1/\log_2(4/3)$ from NAE three-circuit products, which is a different statement outside this page range.

name: walsh_crosspolytope_batching_insufficient
statement: For $r=2^{2t}$ let $H$ be Walsh-Hadamard and $A_r=\{\pm H_{*j}:1\le j\le r\}$ (tag 30), a fully closed crosspolytope fibre with projective full dual $\{\frac1r Hv:v\in\{\pm1\}^r\}/\{\pm1\}$. A bent $v$ has full Walsh support, so one admissible form witnesses a single batch containing an entire perfect matching and the exchange (28) is legal with $k=1$. Nevertheless $d_{\rm cb}(A_r)=r-\lfloor\log_2(2r)\rfloor$ for every coordinate basis (tag 31).
notes: DISPROVES the tempting conclusion that after the witness exchange the unselected rows cost only $O(k)$, or only $O(\sum_s c_s)$, residual directions. NOT a counterexample to linear rigidity: here $\ell=r-\log_2(2r)$, so (31) is exactly of order $\ell$. Moral (S1 line 573-575): a successful proof must allocate the UNUSED GLOBAL DEFECT after the witness exchange, not just count batches or selected-row atom losses.

name: crosspolytope_quotient_counting_lemma
statement: A residual quotient of dimension $q=r-d$ maps the full dual to at most the $2r$ signed selector images, while a rank-$q$ linear image of the cube has at least $2^q$ images; hence $2^q\le2r$, i.e. $d\ge r-\lfloor\log_2(2r)\rfloor$. The matching upper construction attains equality.
notes: Clean reusable lower-bound technique: count images of the cube under the quotient against the number of available signed selector classes.

name: rooted_nae_cycle_fibre
statement: For $n\ge4$, $A_n=\{(a,b_1,\dots,b_n)\in\{\pm1\}^{n+1}: a+b_i+b_{i+1}\in\{\pm1\}\ \forall i\}$ with cyclic indices (tag 32). On the half $a=1$ the vertices with $b_i=1$ form an independent set of $C_n$; the other half is antipodal. Hence $|A_n|=2L_n$ and $\ell(A_n)=n-\log_2 L_n$ (tag 33), $L_n$ the $n$th Lucas number. The fibre is full closed with projective full dual exactly $D_n=\{A,B_i,C_i\}$, $A=e_0$, $B_i=e_i$, $C_i=e_0+e_i+e_{i+1}$ (tag 34).
notes: Ambient rank $r=n+1$, so $\ell=(n+1)-\log_2(2L_n)=n-\log_2 L_n$. VERIFIED: $L_{13}=521$, $\ell(A_{13})=3.97486\ldots$; $|D_n|=2n+1$.

name: rooted_nae_cycle_exact_dcb
statement: For every $n\ge4$, $\boxed{d_{\rm cb}(A_n)=d_{\rm geo}(A_n)=\lceil n/3\rceil}$. Tag (35).
notes: Uniform in $n$; the proof does not depend on enumeration. This is the exact solution of a genuine high-corank cyclic family, in precisely the activation-and-connector form the recursive programme needs.

name: binary_quotient_lemma_S_n
statement: Put $\mathcal S_n=\{0\}\cup\{u_i\}\cup\{u_i+u_{i+1}\}\subseteq\mathbb F_2^n$. For every $w$-dimensional subspace $W$, $\boxed{|\mathcal S_n/W|\ge2n+1-3w}$ (tag 36). For a real signed-difference residual $R$ of dimension $d$, replace $R$ by the rational span $R_0\subseteq R$ of its actual class witnesses ($d_0=\dim R_0\le d$) and reduce the saturated lattice $R_0\cap\mathbb Z^{n+1}$ modulo two; signed equality becomes ordinary coset equality, giving $k_{D_n}(R)\ge2n+1-3d_0\ge2n+1-3d$ (tag 37).
notes: Proof of (36): choose $n-w$ coordinate images forming a quotient basis; removing the other $w$ cycle vertices destroys at most $2w$ cycle edges, so at least $n-2w$ distinct weight-two basis sums remain, plus zero and the $n-w$ singleton images. The REAL-to-$\mathbb F_2$ passage (saturated lattice mod 2) is the reusable trick; it is what makes a real residual bound follow from a binary counting bound.

name: rooted_nae_selector_upper_construction
statement: Choose an independent dominating set $U\subseteq C_n$ of size $d=\lceil n/3\rceil$ whose cyclic gaps all have length two or three; put $L_u=A+B_u$ and $R=\operatorname{span}\{L_u:u\in U\}$ (tag 38a). Orient the cycle; in every gap $u-v-u'$ choose $B_v,C_v$, in every gap $u-v-w-u'$ choose $B_v,C_v,C_w$. With $A$ these are $n+1$ full-dual forms forming a coordinate basis (backward substitution: $B_{u'}$ occurs uniquely in the last $C$-form of the preceding gap). Modulo $R$: $B_u\equiv-A$, $C_u\equiv B_v$, and $B_w\equiv C_w$ in a length-three gap (tag 38b).
notes: Every member of $D_n$ has a signed representative in this basis and every selector residual lies in the independent $d$-space $R$, proving $d_{\rm cb}\le d$. Matching lower-bound counting: cliques of $C_n-U$ number at most $1+(n-|U|)+(n-2|U|)=2n+1-3|U|\le n+1$ (tag 38).

name: rooted_nae_activation_cell_inequality
statement: For $Z_u=1_{\{L_u\ne0\}}$ and every $z\in\{0,1\}^U$, $\boxed{|(A_n)_z|\le2^{\,n+1-d-|z|}}$ (tag 38c). Consequently $|A_n|/2^{n+1}\le(3/4)^d$ and $d\le\ell(A_n)/\log_2(4/3)$ (tag 38d).
notes: Proof: on the $a=1$ half, $Z$ records the intersection of an independent set of $C_n$ with $U$. A length-two gap has $2,1,1$ completions according as its two endpoint states have sum $0,1,2$; a length-three gap has $3,2,1$. These are bounded by $2^{g-1-(s+t)/2}$; multiplying over gaps yields $2^{n-d-|z|}$, and antipodality supplies (38c). This is the STRONGER cellwise form the recursive programme wants, not merely a rank bound.

name: rooted_nae_connector_compatibility_38e
statement: If $A$ is treated as the incoming boundary and the $B_i$ as private coordinates, projection sends $L_u$ to the independent private coordinate $B_u$. Therefore $R\cap\operatorname{span}\{A\}=0$ (tag 38e): the optimal cyclic certificate is connector-compatible with no boundary surcharge.
notes: This is a POSITIVE absorption instance: zero connector intersection, so absorption holds trivially with $R_<=0$. Contrast the NAE STAR, where absorption fails at $R_<=0$. Both are NAE structures; the difference is cyclic connector coherence, not sparsity.

name: rooted_nae_path_and_interval_constants
statement: For the rooted-NAE path on $N$ vertices, $d_{\rm cb}=d_{\rm geo}=\lceil(N-1)/3\rceil$ (tag 38f). If its root and two endpoints are boundary and the $m=N-2$ interior vertices are private, there is a boundary-preserving basis with $d_m=\lceil(m+1)/3\rceil$ and $R_m\cap\operatorname{span}W=0$ (tag 38g). For every $m\ge2$, $d_m\le C_{\rm int}L_{Q\mid W}$ with the sharp uniform coefficient $C_{\rm int}=\frac{2}{3-\log_2 5}=2.949539\ldots$ (tag 38h).
notes: VERIFIED: $2/(3-\log_2 5)=2.9495396947\ldots$. The stronger activation coefficient $1/\beta=2.40942\ldots$ holds for $m=2$ and every $m\ge4$; the three-vertex neutral interval ($m=3$) is the genuine five-point cellwise exception. Proofs in rooted_nae_selector_connector_report.md (not reproduced in pp.55-112).

name: one_private_vertex_interval_no_defect_only_bound
statement: For $m=1$ (one private interior vertex), NO defect-only bound is possible: $L_{Q\mid W}$ can tend to zero while one new direction remains. However the block costs zero once its two boundary residuals have been ancestor-paid.
notes: CRITICAL for the shape of (41): this is why the absorption clause cannot be dropped from the statement -- it is forced into it, not optional. It also shows the two-regime structure: defect-poor blocks can never be charged locally, but they admit exactly-absorbed alternatives once ancestors have paid. Note the caveat 'once its two boundary residuals have been ancestor-paid' -- the bookkeeping semantics matter.

name: rooted_nae_dual_matroid_three_connected
statement: The real full-dual matroid on $D_n$ is genuinely three-connected. A dual representation is $t=\sum_i e_i$, $p_i=e_i$, $q_i=e_i+e_{i+1}$. A run-count proof shows every partition $(X,Y)$ with $|X|,|Y|\ge2$ satisfies $r(X)+r(Y)-n\ge2$; every dual column is nonzero and deleting any one column leaves rank $n$, ruling out singleton one-separations.
notes: Run-count proof lives in rigidity_attack_report.md, not reproduced here. This object exists to certify that the family below is genuinely three-connected, which is what makes it a counterexample rather than a degenerate case.

name: three_connected_ceiling_lemma_disproved
statement: The candidate '$d_{\rm cb}(A)\le\lceil\ell(A)\rceil$ for three-connected full-dual blocks' is FALSE. Already $n=13$ gives $d_{\rm cb}(A_{13})=d_{\rm geo}(A_{13})=5>\lceil13-\log_2 521\rceil=4$ (tag 39); every $n\equiv0\pmod 6$, $n\ge42$ gives an infinite counterexample subfamily. Equivalently, the fixed-$q$ evaluation-Rado proposal fails in genuine three-connected blocks.
notes: VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: $\ell(A_{13})=13-\log_2 521=3.97486$, $\lceil\cdot\rceil=4$, while $\lceil13/3\rceil=5$. Consequence stated by S1: three-connectivity cannot be used as a ZERO-WORK ceiling certificate; a high-corank block must pay a positive entropy cost internally. It does NOT threaten an absolute linear theorem.

name: rooted_nae_ratio_limit_1_0902
statement: $\dfrac{d_{\rm cb}(A_n)}{\ell(A_n)}\longrightarrow\dfrac{1}{3(1-\log_2\varphi)}=1.090186\ldots$ as $n\to\infty$, $\varphi$ the golden ratio. Tag (40).
notes: VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: $\log_2\varphi=0.6942419$, $1/(3\cdot0.3057581)=1.0901865$. Finite values approach from ABOVE: $n=4$ gives $2/1.19265=1.6769$; $n=13$ gives $5/3.97486=1.2579$. So this family forces any valid absolute $C$ in (3) to satisfy $C\ge1.2579$ at $n=13$ and $C\ge1.0902$ asymptotically. It is a LOWER bound on $C$ from one family only, not a floor for the whole class (the S6 p.113 NAE three-circuit floor $C\ge2.40942$ is a separate, stronger statement outside this page range).

name: audit_ledger_five_components_S1
statement: S1's integrated ledger: (i) affine $12+3/3+12$ coupling -- PASS, closes $m=19$ profiles $(2,2,3,12),(2,2,12,3)$ and the cited $m=18$ $\{1,2\}$-line uses; (ii) rank-three shared homogenizer -- PASS, all $m=8$ high normal forms have exact rank-two residual certificates, $m\le7$ intrinsic closure complete; (iii) higher-corank global bridge -- NEW THEOREM $d_{\rm cb}\le9\cdot4^\ell+\ell$; (iv) bounded-congestion high corank -- PASS, new linear theorem $(2\kappa+1)L$; (v) three-connected ceiling lemma -- DISPROVED, replacement PASS (rooted-NAE cycles).

name: affine_12plus3_upper_state_sets
statement: $B_0=\{\eta\in\{\pm1\}^{12}:\sum_i\eta_i=0\}$, $B_2=\{\eta\in\{\pm1\}^{12}:\sum_i\eta_i=2\}$, so $|B_0|=924$, $|B_2|=792$. $M=\{\xi\in\{\pm1\}^3:\sum_j\xi_j=1\}=\{\xi^{(1)},\xi^{(2)},\xi^{(3)}\}$, the three one-minority states. Up to reorientation and reversing the adjacent slice, $\Omega_0=B_0\times M$ ($|\Omega_0|=2772$) and $\Omega_1=(B_0\times\{\xi^{(1)},\xi^{(2)}\})\cup(B_2\times\{\xi^{(3)}\})$ ($|\Omega_1|=2640$). Tag (4).
source: dossier p.57 (S1 lines 100-108); dossier pp.74-75 (S2 lines 41-68)

name: upper_12plus3_dichotomy
statement: Consider either ordering of a twelve-coordinate layer and a three-coordinate layer in an adapted rank-four flag. If their joint affine fibre has more than $2592$ literal sign assignments, then EITHER the coefficient row space contains a four-coordinate relation with four equal nonzero magnitudes, OR the literal upper state set is $\Omega_0$ or $\Omega_1$ after the stated normalizations. Every target is arbitrary.
notes: TARGET-UNIFORM: the target is arbitrary real; no relation between the lower-row statistic and the chosen upper target is assumed (S2 lines 162-164). Independently audited PASS.

name: scalar_gaps_target_uniform
statement: For twelve nonzero coefficients, an affine atom which is not the central atom of twelve equal magnitudes has size at most $792$. Unequal-magnitude case: reorient positively and condition on an unequal pair; its four signed sums are distinct, and the ten-coordinate subsets hitting one of the four required targets form a four-Sperner family, so their total is at most $\binom{10}{5}+2\binom{10}{4}+\binom{10}{3}=252+210+210+120=792$. Equal magnitudes with noncentral target: largest noncentral layer is $\binom{12}{5}=792$. A three-sign affine atom has size three only for three equal magnitudes at a one-minority target; otherwise at most two.
notes: VERIFIED: $252+420+120=792$. Consequence: more than $2592$ joint states forces both own-layer rows to be equimodular, since otherwise the joint count is at most $3\cdot792=2376$ or $2\cdot924=1848$. The four-Sperner step is the reusable device.

name: twelve_outermost_four_level_reduction
statement: With equations $\sum_i\eta_i=0$ and $\sum_i b_i\eta_i+\sum_j\xi_j=u$: if some $\Delta=b_i-b_j\notin\{0,\pm1,\pm2,\pm3\}$, conditioning on the other ten balanced signs gives at most $252\cdot3+420\cdot3=2016<2592$. Above the threshold every pairwise difference lies in $\{0,\pm1,\pm2,\pm3\}$, and adding a multiple of the balanced row puts all twelve $b_i$ on the four consecutive levels $0,1,2,3$.
notes: VERIFIED: $252\cdot3+420\cdot3=2016$. In the $\binom{10}{5}=252$ zero-remaining-sum cases the two opposite completions require three-sign sums separated by $2\Delta$, so at most one can occur (total multiplicity $\le3$); in the remaining $2\binom{10}{6}=420$ completable cases the distinguished pair is fixed. This is the ARBITRARY-REAL reduction the C++ checker does NOT prove.

name: profile_convolution_455_above_2592
statement: The exact 455-profile convolution has only these profiles above $2592$: (a) all twelve coefficients on one level, maximum $2772$, attained only at the two one-minority triple targets; (b) eleven coefficients on one level and one on an adjacent level, maximum $2772$, attained at the central four-sign target. Case (a) gives $\Omega_0$; in case (b) subtracting the balanced twelve-row leaves a unit row on the three $\xi$'s and the one exceptional $\eta$ (the four-coordinate relation). Every other profile has at most $2436$ states. Tag (5): 455 profiles, 10 high, $\max=2772$, runner-up $=2436$.
source: dossier p.57 (S1 lines 114-118); dossier p.77 (S2 lines 132-143); dossier p.82 (S2 lines 367-374)

CAUTION: this '2436 runner-up' is the profile runner-up and is a DIFFERENT quantity from the 792 affine-atom runner-up; the retracted number was 744.

name: three_outermost_binomial_triples
statement: When the three signs are outermost, the outer triple must be the three one-minority states; the next row has twelve equal own coefficients and its three shifted targets request three binomial slices of twelve equal signs. The only nonzero slice sizes are $924,792,495,220,66,12,1$, and the only sorted triples with sum greater than $2592$ are $(924,924,924)$ and $(924,924,792)$. These are exactly $\Omega_0$ and $\Omega_1$. Tag (6).
source: dossier p.77 (S2 lines 146-164); dossier p.57 (S1 lines 120-124)
notes: Slice sizes are $\binom{12}{6},\binom{12}{7},\binom{12}{8},\binom{12}{9},\binom{12}{10},\binom{12}{11},\binom{12}{12}$ = 924,792,495,220,66,12,1. The reversed calculation independently returned only these two triples.

name: N_s_conditional_pair_completion_count
statement: Let $a\ne0$, $T(\eta,\xi)=\sum_i b_i\eta_i+\sum_j c_j\xi_j$, and for an arbitrary real target $s$ put $N_s(T;\Omega)=\#\{(\eta,\xi,\sigma_1,\sigma_2):(\eta,\xi)\in\Omega,\ T(\eta,\xi)+a(\sigma_1+\sigma_2)=s\}$.
notes: The equal pair $(\sigma_1,\sigma_2)$ contributes the multiplicity kernel $(1,2,1)$. Conditioning on LITERAL upper states is what permits arbitrary dependence of the lower row on every upper coordinate.

name: affine_12plus3_conditional_pair_lemma
statement: $T$ nonconstant on $\Omega_0\Rightarrow N_s(T;\Omega_0)\le4788$; $T$ nonconstant on $\Omega_1\Rightarrow N_s(T;\Omega_1)\le4776$; uniformly in $a,s,b,c$. Tag (7).
source: dossier pp.57-58 (S1 lines 131-137); dossier pp.78-79 (S2 lines 183-248)
notes: VERIFIED: if some $b_i\ne b_j$, conditioning on the other ten signs gives $\binom{10}{5}\cdot3+2\binom{10}{6}\cdot2=252\cdot3+420\cdot2=1596$, so $N_s(\Omega_0)\le3\cdot1596=4788$ and $N_s(\Omega_1)\le2\cdot1596+2\binom{12}{7}=3192+1584=4776$. If all $b_i$ equal, $T$ is constant on each twelve-slice block and the bounds are strictly smaller: $\Omega_0\le5\cdot924=4620$; $\Omega_1\le3\cdot924+2\cdot792=4356$ (balanced centers differ) or $4\cdot924+792=4488$ (balanced centers agree, adjacent differs). All five numbers reproduced exactly.

name: constancy_alternative_row_space_conclusion
statement: Constancy is a complete alternative, not merely a counting label. On $\Omega_0$, exchanges inside $B_0$ force $b=\beta\mathbf1_{12}$ and comparison of the three minority states forces $c=\gamma\mathbf1_3$, so the old part of the lower row lies in the span of the two upper rows. On $\Omega_1$, with $R_\xi=(0,\mathbf1_3)$, $R_{\eta,p}=(\mathbf1_{12},p)$ and slice sums $s_j=q-p\cdot\xi^{(j)}\in\{0,0,2\}$, slice exchanges give $b=\beta\mathbf1_{12}$ and a linear form constant on the three minority states has three equal coefficients, so $(b,c)=\beta R_{\eta,p}+\lambda R_\xi$. Subtracting cancels all fifteen upper coordinates, leaving a nonzero row supported on at most two old coordinates -- contradicting projective simplicity.
source: dossier pp.79-80 (S2 lines 253-296); dossier p.58 (S1 lines 150-153)
notes: Also handled with affine targets tracked: a violating atom forces the equal pair to use its central two-completion value, and the same subtraction cancels the residual target. S2 line 295: 'no homogenizing-coordinate shortcut is being used.'

name: m19_m18_endpoint_closure_arithmetic
statement: At $m=19$ a violation would have more than $H_{19}=\frac{81}{4096}2^{19}=10368$ states; the two lower two-sign layers have scalar multiplicity at most four, so the upper fifteen signs must exceed $2592$. Applying the dichotomy: the four-coordinate alternative gives $d_{\rm geo}\le3$; in an $\Omega_s$ alternative, unequal magnitudes give at most one completion per upper state, equal magnitudes with nonconstant statistic give at most $4788$, and the last pair contributes at most two, so $2\cdot4788=9576<10368$ (tag 8). At $m=18$, $4788<5184=\frac{81}{4096}2^{18}$ (tag 9).
source: dossier p.58 (S1 lines 155-167); dossier pp.80-81 (S2 lines 298-333)
notes: VERIFIED: $81\cdot2^{19}/4096=10368$; $81\cdot2^{18}/4096=5184$; $2\cdot4788=9576$. Closes $m=19$ profiles $(2,2,3,12)$ and $(2,2,12,3)$, and validates the $m=18$ invocation on an ordinary line of type $\{1,2\}$ (singleton contributes at most one, pair at most two, so the same $2592$ threshold applies). name: last_five_profiles_sharp_six_argument
statement: For the separate profiles $(2,12,2,3)$ and $(12,2,2,3)$, a violation forces the absolute joint maximum six in the last $2+3$ signs. Equality forces the outer triple to be its three one-minority states and the pair to have two central completions over every state. If the pair row is $\xi_1+\xi_2+p\cdot\eta=t'$, then $p\cdot\eta=t'$ on all three minority states, whence $p_1=p_2=p_3=\lambda$ and $t'=\lambda\tau$; subtracting the triple row leaves $\xi_1+\xi_2=0$, a genuine old support-two relation.

name: floating_point_in_exact_checkers_defect

The proof-relevant part of affine_shared_h_m8_normalforms.cpp is safer (primal_forms, rank_i, quotient_classes are integer); its numerical RREF key in geo_family_at_most only skips purported duplicate planes and cannot create a false positive. name: local_three_edge_relation_completeness
statement: Let the saturated quotient have $m+1-(m-2)=3$ units of class excess; a signed spanning forest of its nontrivial classes has exactly three edges. Restriction is injective on $\widehat R$ when $h\notin\widehat R$, so two old-old edge residuals span the two-dimensional admissible space and one further edge joins $h$ to an old form. An unsigned three-edge forest is, after removing isolated vertices, exactly one of $3K_2$, $P_3+K_2$, $P_4$, $K_{1,3}$ (tag 10), and a signed forest can be switched so all three edges are ordinary differences. With edge evaluations $d_1,d_2,d_3$ satisfying $d_i/2\in\{0,\pm1\}$ on the antipodal atom, a primitive dependence $\alpha$ is the cross product of two rows of $\{0,\pm1\}^3$, giving exactly sixteen normalized triples.
source: dossier p.86 (S3 lines 105-125); dossier p.58 (S1 line 179)
notes: The sixteen: $(1,\pm1,\pm1),(1,\pm1,\pm2),(1,\pm2,\pm1),(2,\pm1,\pm1)$. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: cross products of ternary rows with all entries nonzero give exactly 16 canonical lines, matching this list. This proves the coefficient search is EXHAUSTIVE, not a bounded-coefficient heuristic. If one coefficient is zero, the two survivors have equal magnitude; adjacent forest edges then telescope to a support-two row or force three sign forms to coincide projectively, leaving only two disjoint edges (the balanced support-four relation treated analytically).

Such a coincidence would be a second supported relation on the endpoints, which is excluded, so at most two local extras are possible.

name: m8_AAB_graph_structure_and_count
statement: For five-sign support with repeated planar types $A,A,B$, let $G$ be the graph on the five supported columns with $ij\in E$ when $u_i+u_j=2T$, $T\in\{\pm B,\pm2A\pm B\}$. Each edge contributes at most two solutions, so a total of at least fourteen implies $|E(G)|\ge7$; Mantel gives a triangle, and a disconnected graph on five vertices has at most six edges, so $G$ is connected. Relabelling a triangle $0,1,2$ with edge labels $a,b,c$ determines $u_0=a+b-c$, $u_1=a+c-b$, $u_2=b+c-a$ uniquely; a spanning tree to vertices $3,4$ has exactly two forms, giving the count $6^3\bigl((3\cdot6)^2+3\cdot6\cdot6\bigr)=93{,}312$.
notes: VERIFIED: $216\cdot(324+108)=216\cdot432=93312$. There is no remaining continuous parameter -- the triangle determines $u_0,u_1,u_2$ and every attachment equation determines the next $u_i$. Sorting the five $u_i$ quotients only by an allowed $S_5$-symmetry, so the reduction to $2{,}934$ multisets is LOSSLESS. This is the argument that upgrades a finite enumeration into a complete classification.

name: zero_gale_column_deletion_lemma
statement: Suppose $c_1=0$; write $C'=(c_2,\dots,c_m)$, $S'_t=\{x'\in\{\pm1\}^{m-1}:C'x'=t\}$, $W'=\ker C'$. Then $S_t=\{\pm1\}\times S'_t$ and $|S_t|/2^m=|S'_t|/2^{m-1}$ (tag 4); moreover every dimension-$d$ residual certificate for the reduced family lifts to a dimension-$d$ certificate for the original, so $d_{\rm geo}(F')\le2\Rightarrow d_{\rm geo}(F)\le2$ (tag 5). Corollary: deleting all zero Gale columns preserves the affine atom density, and if the unreduced family is projectively simple with $d_{\rm geo}(F)=3$ then the reduced family also has $d_{\rm geo}=3$.
source: dossier pp.104-105 (S5 lines 57-108); dossier p.91 (S3 lines 288-290); dossier p.60 (S1 lines 227-228)
notes: Proof: $W=\mathbb Re_1\oplus W'$, $r=1+r'$; regarding $R'$ as $0\oplus R'$, the reduced forms occupy $\le r'$ classes and the free coordinate $e_1^*$ adds at most one, so $k_F(R)\le r'+1=r$. The corollary's exactness uses that three signed forest edges always give a residual of dimension $\le3$ with class excess three. The other hypotheses descend too: projective simplicity is inherited by a subfamily; affine spanning descends under the projection; coordinate-fullness descends through the free product.

name: free_product_full_dual_decomposition
statement: Let $A=\{\pm1\}\times A'$ span $\mathbb R\oplus V'$ and suppose $g(s,x)=as+g'(x)$ is sign-valued on $A$. For every $x\in A'$ both $a+g'(x)$ and $-a+g'(x)$ lie in $\{\pm1\}$; therefore either $a=0$ and $g'$ is sign-valued on $A'$, or $|a|=1$ and $g'$ vanishes on the spanning set $A'$, so $g=\pm s$. Hence the projective full dual of a free product is exactly the disjoint union of the free coordinate and the full dual of the reduced factor.
notes: Consequence: deleting or reinserting free coordinates creates NO hidden full-dual form. This is what justifies every occurrence of 'after zero Gale columns are deleted' in the finite reduction -- a hypothesis-preservation lemma, not just a counting one.

name: spanning_homogenization_lemma
statement: If $S_t$ affinely spans its expected $r$-dimensional affine solution space, then $\widehat A_t=\{(x,1):x\in S_t\}\cup\{(-x,-1):x\in S_t\}=\widehat W\cap\{\pm1\}^{m+1}$ linearly spans $\widehat W=\ker[C\mid-t]$. Proof: fix $x_0\in S_t$; the differences $x-x_0$ span $\ker C$, so the lifts span $\ker C\times\{0\}$ and $(x_0,1)$, whose sum has dimension $r+1=m-2=\dim\widehat W$.
source: dossier p.106 (S5 lines 128-142); tags (2),(3) on dossier pp.103-104
notes: $\dim\widehat W=m-2=r+1$ because $C$ has row rank three. 'Coordinate-full' means the displayed projective forms $\{\widehat f_1,\dots,\widehat f_m,h\}$ are the ENTIRE projective full dual of $\widehat A_t$.

name: intrinsic_cube_model_closure_lemma
statement: Assume affine spanning and coordinate-full homogenization; put $R=\dim\widehat W=m-2$, $M=m+1$. Then after a linear choice of intrinsic coordinates, $\widehat A_t$ becomes an antipodal spanning subset $A\subset\{\pm1\}^R$ (tag 6) which is full closed and whose projective full dual satisfies $|D(A)|=M=R+3$ (tag 7).
notes: Proof: choose $R$ independent full-dual members as a basis and let $\Phi(w)=(g_1(w),\dots,g_R(w))$ (tag 8), a linear isomorphism mapping $\widehat A_t$ into the intrinsic cube. The $M$ displayed homogenized coordinate forms are projectively distinct (if $\widehat f_i=\pm h$ on $\widehat W$, restriction to $U=\ker h=\ker C\times\{0\}$ would give $f_i=0$ on $\ker C$, contradicting old projective simplicity). Closure: if $y\in\operatorname{cl}(A)$ and $w=\Phi^{-1}(y)$, every displayed coordinate of $w$ is a sign, so $w\in\widehat W\cap\{\pm1\}^M=\widehat A_t$.

name: restriction_inequality_d_geo

name: forced_exceptional_plane_prop_4_1
statement: Assume (1) $S_t$ affinely spans its expected affine flat; (2) the old coordinate family is projectively simple; (3) the homogenization is coordinate-full; (4) $d_{\rm geo}(F)=3$; (5) the homogeneous relation-corank-three theorem gives $d_{\rm geo}(\widehat F)\le2$ (tag 11). Then $d_{\rm geo}(\widehat F)=2$ and EVERY optimal homogenized residual plane $\widehat R$ has the saturated shared-$h$ pattern: $\boxed{k_{\widehat F}(\widehat R)=r+1,\ h\notin\widehat R,\ [h]_{\widehat R}\text{ contains an old form},\ \dim S=2}$ (tag 12), with no additional merger after restriction, where $S=\operatorname{span}\{f_i-\sigma f_j:f_i-\sigma f_j\in\widehat R|_{\ker h}\}$ (tag 13).
notes: Each alternative is killed by producing an old residual of dimension $\le2$: an optimal plane leaving $\le r$ classes descends directly; if the $h$-class contains no old form, deleting $h$ removes one class; if $h\in\widehat R$, restriction loses one residual dimension and the remaining merger costs at most one; if restriction causes any extra merger; and if $\dim S<2$, adjoin one old signed difference between two remaining classes. Quantifier (S5 line 301): under old distance three EVERY optimal plane must satisfy (12), and it is enough to select ONE and apply the exclusion.

name: shared_h_integration_thm_4_2
statement: Assume the completed homogeneous relation-corank-three density theorem and the shared-$h$ structural estimates. Under affine spanning, projective simplicity, and coordinate-full homogenization: $d_{\rm geo}(F)=3\ \Longrightarrow\ |S_t|/2^m\le 27/512$ (tag 15).
notes: CONDITIONAL on the completed homogeneous corank-three density theorem, which is NOT proved in pp.55-112. Proof structure: delete zero Gale columns (Cor 2.2); homogenization preserves density exactly, $|\widehat A_t|/2^{m+1}=2|S_t|/2^{m+1}=\rho$ (tag 17); Prop 4.1 forces the saturated pattern; the shared-$h$ relation analysis produces a row of $\widehat C$ containing $h$, balanced on four or six coordinates, so after setting $h=1$ its old support has size $q=3$ or $q=5$ with three or ten admissible support states. Case split: long-direction estimate for Gale multiplicity $\ge3$; with multiplicity $\le2$, flag bounds handle $m\ge12$, planar conditional spectra handle $m=9,10,11$, the exact normal-form checker handles $m=8$, and Section 3 plus the closed-fibre enumeration handle $m\le7$.

name: shared_h_exact_checker_design
statement: shared_h_exact_checker.py: an exact certificate checker for the shared-$h$ rank-three endpoint using NO floating-point operation -- linear algebra over $\mathbb Q$ via fractions.Fraction, finite fibres and closures represented by bit masks. Modes: `local` (the 16 primitive three-edge relations on four forest shapes), `m8` (all three $m=8$ normal-form families and residual certificates), `full` (all antipodal full-closed fibres through intrinsic rank five), `all` (default).
source: dossier p.92 (S4 lines 1-12); dossier p.111 (S5 lines 303-335)
notes: Core routines: qrank (exact Gauss-Jordan over $\mathbb Q$), solve_square, exact_full_dual, canonical_line, difference_directions, quotient_classes, residual_certificate, projectively_simple, primal_forms, planar_spectrum. This is the canonical replacement for the floating-point C++ routines flagged in S3 section 6.1.

name: exact_full_dual_algorithm
statement: exact_full_dual(points): compute $r=\operatorname{qrank}(\text{points})$, greedily keep $r$ coordinates on which the projection still has rank $r$, take $r$ independent projected points as a basis, and for each tail in $\{\pm1\}^{r-1}$ set values $=(1,\text{tail})$, solve $Bh=\text{values}$ exactly over $\mathbb Q$, and accept the form iff $|\langle x,h\rangle|=1$ for EVERY projected point $x$. Returns the accepted value-vectors as the projective full dual in evaluation coordinates.
notes: Normalization to first evaluation $=1$ is exactly the projective quotient by $\pm1$; enumerating tails is complete because a full-dual form is determined by its values on a basis of the fibre. This makes the full dual computable exactly, which is the pivot on which the whole finite programme rests.

name: residual_certificate_search_algorithm
statement: quotient_classes(forms, residual): $i\sim j$ iff for some sign $\sigma$, $\operatorname{qrank}(\text{residual}\cup\{f_i-\sigma f_j\})=\operatorname{qrank}(\text{residual})$. residual_certificate(forms, target): if $|\text{forms}|\le r$ return the trivial certificate; otherwise enumerate all canonical signed-difference directions $f_i-\sigma f_j$ and, for $d=1,\dots,\text{target}$, test every $d$-subset of independent directions, returning the first whose quotient has at most $r=\operatorname{qrank}(\text{forms})$ classes.
notes: Exhaustive over signed-difference residuals of dimension $\le$ target, so a NEGATIVE result (None) is a proof that $d_{\rm geo}>$ target within the signed-difference class -- this is what makes the checker a certificate producer in both directions.

name: primal_forms_integer_coordinate_rows
statement: primal_forms(cols): given $m$ columns in $\mathbb Z^3$, pick three with nonzero $3\times3$ determinant as pivots; for each free index $j$, set $\text{forms}[j][z]=\det(\text{pivot matrix})$ and $\text{forms}[\text{pivot}_k][z]=\det$ of the pivot matrix with row $k$ replaced by $-\text{cols}[j]$. Returns exact INTEGER coordinate rows for the coordinate forms on $\ker C$.
notes: Cramer/adjugate construction -- the integer analogue of the $g=\operatorname{adj}(B)v/\det B$ repair S3 prescribes for the floating-point C++ routines. It is why the $m=8$ part of the checker was already safe.

name: ell_defect_and_d_cb

name: weighted_two_shadow_compression_thm1
statement: Theorem 1 (S6). Let K = R, or K = F_p with p > r odd. Let h_a in K^r and S = {x in {+-1}^r : h_a.x in {+-1} for every a}, |S| = 2^{r-ell}. Discard rows equal to signed coordinate forms; for each remaining row let E_a = supp h_a, so |E_a| >= 2. There is a set C subset [r] with |C| <= C_0*4^ell (tag 8) and |E_a \ C| <= 1 for every a (tag 9). One may take an absolute numerical C_0, for example C_0 = 32.
source: dossier p.115 (S6 lines 103-129); audit p.128 (S7 lines 30-46)
notes: S7 sharpens the admissible constant to C_0 = 9. Improves the old two-shadow core size from O((1+ell)4^ell) to O(4^ell). NO full-closure and NO antipodality hypothesis is used. Field condition p > r odd is required (it feeds u <= r < p in the finite-group LO step).

name: psi_two_target_atom_bound
statement: psi(u) = min{3/4, 2^{1-u}*C(u, floor(u/2))} <= min{3/4, 2/sqrt(u)} (tag 12). For u = 2 the 3/4 bound is the nondegenerate-parallelogram bound; for u >= 3 it is the ordinary two-atom Littlewood-Offord bound. Over F_p invoke the finite-group one-point Littlewood-Offord theorem: when u < p and all coefficients are nonzero, each atom is at most the central-binomial mass; a union bound over the two targets gives the same psi.
source: dossier p.116 (S6 lines 174-186); audit pp.131-132 (S7 lines 139-184)
notes: The bound must be uniform in the target center b, in the coefficients, and in all earlier block values - all three quantifiers are used by the reverse-exposure argument.

name: reverse_exposure_triangular_product
statement: Batching: at step s pick a still-present matching pair P_t, pick a witness row E_s containing it, and remove B_s = {u : P_u still present and P_u cap E_s nonempty}, a_s = |B_s| (tag 10). With V_s the union of pair endpoints in B_s and U_s = E_s cap V_s: the U_s are pairwise disjoint, E_s contains at least a_s+1 coordinates of U_s, and E_t cap U_s = empty for t < s. Conditioning on coordinates outside the union of U_s and peeling U_k,...,U_1 in reverse gives Pr(h_s.X in {+-1} | earlier) <= psi(a_s+1) (tag 11), hence 2^{-ell} <= prod_s psi(a_s+1) (tag 13).
notes: S7 confirms this is a triangular CONDITIONAL-EXPECTATION product, not an independence claim, and requires the proof be rewritten with the disjoint U_s and an explicit reverse conditional expectation. Rows E_s may still involve variables in earlier U_t; those are held as arbitrary parameters, which is why target uniformity is needed.

name: batching_entropy_arithmetic
statement: Put c_s = -log_2 psi(a_s+1). Then c_s >= beta := log_2(4/3), sum_s c_s <= ell, and a_s+1 <= 4*4^{c_s} (tag 14). With C_* = sum_s c_s and b = 4^beta = 16/9, (sum_s 4^{c_s})/4^{C_*} = sum_s 4^{-(C_*-c_s)} <= m*b^{-(m-1)} <= 9/8 (tag 15), maximized at m = 2 and equal to 1 at m = 1. Since C_* <= ell this gives N = sum_s a_s <= (9/2)*4^ell (tag 16), and taking the matching endpoints as C gives |C| = 2N <= 9*4^ell.
source: dossier p.117 (S6 lines 194-222); audit pp.132-133 (S7 lines 187-235)
notes: m is the number of batches. Monotonicity check (S7): (m+1)b^{-m} / (m b^{-(m-1)}) = (m+1)/(mb) < 1 for m >= 2. The N = 0 case must be separated before the weighted sum. The key gain over the old proof: a dense row meeting many matching pairs is charged its full O(a_s^{-1/2}) LO atom instead of one 3/4 factor times its support size.

name: entropy_sharpened_star_core_thm2
statement: Theorem 2 (S6). Assume in addition that S is antipodal and nonempty. For the fixed input coordinate basis, d(H) <= C_0*4^ell + ell (tag 17). Consequently, for a full-closed fibre, d_cb(A) <= C_0*4^{ell(A)} + ell(A) (tag 18).
source: dossier pp.117-118 (S6 lines 229-242); audit pp.134-135 (S7 lines 240-301)
notes: Improves the old residual-rank bound |C| + 2^{|C|} to |C| + ell. With C_0 = 9 this reads d(H) <= 9*4^ell + ell. No full-closure assumption is used except when (18) is read as a statement about the entire full dual. S7: antipodality is automatic for a nonempty compatibility set defined by homogeneous two-sided constraints h_a.x in {+-1}.

name: conditionally_free_coordinate_dichotomy
statement: After Theorem 1 each row is h_a(x) = q_a(x_C) + lambda_a*x_j for at most one j outside C (tag 19). Call j conditionally free if for SOME realized core value X_C = c both signs of X_j occur among points of S having that same core value. If a row uses a conditionally free j, evaluating on two such points gives q_a(c)+lambda_a and q_a(c)-lambda_a both in {+-1}; since lambda_a is nonzero these are the two distinct signs, so q_a(c) = 0 and lambda_a = +-1 (tag 20). Assign the row to the signed coordinate lambda_a*x_j; its residual is supported on C.
source: dossier p.118 (S6 lines 246-271); audit p.134 (S7 lines 243-262)
notes: 'Distinct' requires characteristic zero or odd characteristic - this is where the odd-p hypothesis enters Theorem 2 (as opposed to Theorem 1, where it enters via LO).

name: never_free_vector_determinism_N0_bound
statement: Let N_0 be the outside coordinates that are never conditionally free. For every realized core pattern each X_j, j in N_0, has at most one possible sign, so the WHOLE VECTOR X_{N_0} (not merely each coordinate separately) is a deterministic function of X_C: H(X_C, X_{N_0}) = H(X_C) (tag 21). For uniform X on S, r - ell = H(X) <= H(X_C) + r - |C| - |N_0| (tag 22), hence |N_0| <= ell - (|C| - H(X_C)) <= ell (tag 23).
source: dossier pp.118-119 (S6 lines 273-301); audit p.134 (S7 lines 263-283)
notes: S6 flags this explicitly: 'This is the point at which a naive conditioning argument can go wrong. Equation (21) is valid precisely because never free is required for EVERY realized core pattern.' A per-coordinate version of the argument is false.

name: conditional_exponential_cyclic_block_thm3
statement: Theorem 3 (S6), the connector-ready but exponential estimate. Let (W,Q) be a sign basis on a finite support A with |Q| = q and L = q - H(Q|W) (tag 24). Let Y_a be sign-valued linear forms with private decomposition Y_a = u_a(W) + h_a(Q) (tag 25); boundary-only forms are passed to the parent. There is a private coordinate set C with |C| <= C_0*4^L such that every supp h_a has at most one coordinate outside C, and the private forms admit selectors whose NEW residual rank modulo span W is at most C_0*4^L + L (tag 26).
notes: Proof route: L = E_w[q - log_2|A_w|] (27); choose w_0 with fibre defect <= L; the compatibility set cut out by u_a(w_0)+h_a(Q) in {+-1} contains A_{w_0}, so has density >= 2^{-L}; Theorem 1 is target-uniform and applies VERBATIM to these affine equations. Free/never-free then gives H(Q_{N_0}|W,Q_C) = 0 (28) and |N_0| <= L. Not separately audited by S7 (S7 audits Theorems 1-2 only).

name: thm3_does_not_give_absorption

notes: The precise failure mode: quotient-rank control says nothing about which combinations land in span W. S9's Lemma 2 turns this into an exact kernel criterion.

name: endpoint_component_exponent_ternary_basis_mass
statement: For a rank-r, size-k = r+j component, the ternary basis-mass encoding has exponent -(n-r)*ell + O(d_cb*k + j*log r + r + n) (tag 29). Substituting Theorem 2 gives -(n-r)*ell + O((4^ell + ell)*k + j*log r + r + n) (tag 30).

notes: This is the exact interface at which a deterministic d_cb bound becomes a probabilistic component saving; the coefficient on d_cb is k (component size), which is why an o(log n) coefficient suffices at the endpoint.

name: controlled_range_4l_o_ell_log_n
statement: Uniformly for k = O(n/log n), every component sequence with ell -> infinity and 4^ell = o(ell*log n) (tag 31) has the required exponential component saving: (29) equals -(1-o(1))*(n-r)*ell. Fixed defect was already covered by the star-core theorem.
source: dossier p.121 (S6 lines 405-414); audit verification pp.136-137 (S7 lines 344-377)
notes: S7's explicit arithmetic: r,j <= k gives n-r = n(1-o(1)) and j log r + r + n = O(n); (4^ell+ell)k/((n-r)ell) = O(4^ell/(ell log n) + 1/log n) = o(1); (j log r + r + n)/((n-r)ell) = O(1/ell) = o(1).

name: survivor_defect_threshold_loglog
statement: Pointwise form (S7): if for some fixed c > 0 one has 4^ell/(ell*log n) >= c (tag 35), then 2*ell >= log_2 log n + log_2 ell - O_c(1) (36) and hence ell >= (1/2)log_2 log n + (1/2)log_2 log log n - O_c(1) (37). Equivalently and unambiguously (38): ell <= (1/2)log_2 log n + (1/2)log_2 log log n - omega(1) implies 4^ell = o(ell log n).
source: dossier p.121 (S6 lines 415-421); corrected form pp.137-138 (S7 lines 379-409)
notes: QUANTIFIER CORRECTION, required by S7: S6's tag (32) as written is wrong for oscillating sequences. Failure of the little-o condition only yields c > 0 and an INFINITE SUBSEQUENCE on which (35), hence (37), holds - not the threshold at every index. Cite the pointwise (35) or the subsequence form, never (32) unqualified.
