name: cex_k33_incremental_rigidity
statement: K_{3,3} incremental obstruction: adding the ninth form raises rigidity from one to two while deleting only one antipodal pair (mass ratio 7/8). Hence no deletion-ratio assertion (rigidity increment forces a proportional loss of fibre mass) is available. General K_{p,q} grids also satisfy (17), albeit nonsharply.
notes: Counterexample-audit item 3. Kills deletion-ratio / sequential-rigidity-increment proof strategies; S6's Theorems 1-2 make no such assertion.

name: failed_saturated_optimizer_k3q
statement: Saturated-optimizer failures in K_{3,q}: there is no saturated geometric optimizer and no private collision to invoke. Any proof asking for one fails on this family.
notes: Counterexample-audit item 4. S6's proof deliberately avoids both devices.

name: cex_32_star_treewidth_two_family
statement: The (3,2)-star / treewidth-two family: its density tends to 1/2 while the number of ears is unbounded, yet its actual residual rank remains ONE. The weighted batching survives it by putting all matching pairs met by the shared dense row into one batch and charging that batch its true Littlewood-Offord atom.
notes: Counterexample-audit item 5. This family is exactly why the batching must be WEIGHTED: an unweighted charge of one 3/4 factor per dense row times its support size loses here.

name: crosspolytope_excess_dual_useless
statement: Crosspolytopes: their full dual has exponentially many forms, so excess-dual (dual-cardinality) bounds are useless on them. Here ell = r - Theta(log r), so the exponential bound (17) is intentionally much weaker than the exact crosspolytope certificate and causes no contradiction.
notes: Counterexample-audit item 6. Records that the crosspolytope does not contradict (17) - the contradiction it does produce is against the O(m) residual bootstrap (see one_witness_per_batch_bootstrap_false).

name: failed_axis_subcube_and_sequential_increment
statement: Balanced middle slices and the maximum-axis-subcube failure: no proof may use an axis-aligned subcube extraction or a sequential rigidity increment. S6's argument uses neither.
notes: Counterexample-audit item 7.

name: failed_direct_sum_additivity_of_dcb
statement: Arbitrary direct-sum additivity of d_cb on abstract coordinate families is not available. S6's proof establishes a single GLOBAL residual span instead of assuming additivity.
notes: Counterexample-audit item 8. Relevant to any block-decomposition/telescope argument that wants to add per-block residual ranks.

name: random_dense_row_exponential_barrier
statement: A single row of support s has two-point atom O(s^{-1/2}), so its defect is at least (1/2)log_2 s - O(1) - exactly the scale s = O(4^ell) appearing in (8). Hence the exponential dependence in Theorems 1-2 CANNOT be improved by a support-size argument alone; a linear theorem must use basis exchange or aggregation of the residual row space.
notes: One of the sharpest constraints on the whole program: it names the only two admissible mechanisms for reaching linear-in-defect (basis exchange, residual-row-space aggregation) and rules out support/density counting. Consistency check for the two-shadow theorem, not a counterexample.

name: residual_class_after_thm3
statement: The unresolved deterministic statement is confined to blocks with ALL of: singleton-layer cyclic SCC after every admissible Gale basis exchange; in the homogeneous boundary-closed case relation corank >= 5; in the nonroot case genuinely affine boundary fibres and failure of connector absorption; conditional defect satisfying the threshold (32) while the general basis-mass estimate forces ell*(n-r) < r*j + O(n); no sparse-cyclomatic fundamental graph, no relation-side feedback set of size o(log n), no large disjoint-support matching, no o(log n) ordinary star core, no sufficiently low-rank shared form, and no multiplicative subgroup/coset fibre.
notes: This is the exact residual class the open theorem must cover. Every exclusion is a route already closed elsewhere in the dossier; a candidate counterexample or proof must respect all of them simultaneously.

name: high_corank_connector_rigidity_theorem
statement: THE NAMED GAP (boxed in S6). High-corank connector-rigidity theorem: every cyclic SCC in the residual class has a globally compatible basis/selector certificate satisfying (3), with an ABSOLUTE LINEAR coefficient. Equivalently, one may bypass the decomposition and prove the global selector theorem (1), or the stronger Rado theorem (4), directly. S6: 'This is the irreducible gap: not another scalar endpoint enumeration, but a mass/entropy-weighted basis-exchange theorem for a genuinely high-corank cyclic two-level configuration.'
notes: The coefficient must be at least 2.40942 by the NAE three-circuit products. Proving it is still NOT the conjecture - the Layer-III transfer remains separate.

name: low_corank_induction_does_not_lift
statement: The finite corank-three/four classifications verify only the first local cases of the connector-rigidity assertion and do NOT imply it by induction, for two named reasons: (i) one-new-form ears have zero local rank-corrected entropy, and (ii) nonbinary separator states do not factor.
notes: These two reasons are the concrete obstructions any inductive lift must defeat; a proposed induction that does not address zero-entropy ears and nonbinary separators is already known to fail.

name: simultaneous_pivot_triangular_exchange
statement: Number the batches in deletion order, let h_s be the witness form at batch s, and choose a pivot p_s from the witness matching pair in B_s. Then h_s(p_s) != 0 and h_s(p_t) = 0 for t > s (tag 33), because every pair in a later batch was still present when h_s was chosen so h_s cannot meet either of its endpoints. Hence T = (h_s(p_t))_{1<=s,t<=m} (34) is triangular with nonzero diagonal, and B' = {h_1,...,h_m} union {x_j : j not in {p_1,...,p_m}} (35) is an admissible coordinate basis.
notes: S6: 'This simultaneous exchange lemma is completely correct.' What it does NOT say is that another row is close, modulo a low-rank space, to a member of B'; triangularity concerns only the m-by-m pivot minor of the selected witnesses.

name: walsh_hadamard_fibre_full_closure
statement: Let r = 2^{2t} with coordinates indexed by F_2^{2t}, H the symmetric Walsh-Hadamard matrix H_{a,z} = (-1)^{a.z} with H^2 = rI, and c_z = H e_z in {+-1}^r. The antipodal spanning fibre A_r = {+- c_z} (tag 36) has signed full dual D~(A_r) = {h_v = (1/r)Hv : v in {+-1}^r} (37), with h_v.c_z = v_z (38). A_r is FULLY CLOSED: if x in {+-1}^r satisfies every equation of (37), then y = H^T x has v.y in {+-r} for all sign vectors v (39), so comparing v with its i-th flip gives y_i in {0,+-r}; since ||y||^2 = r||x||^2 = r^2 exactly one coordinate is nonzero, hence x = +- c_z.
notes: The crosspolytope family in its exact form. Full closure is PROVED here, not assumed - this is what makes it admissible as a counterexample against statements quantified over full-closed fibres. |A_r| = 2r, so ell = r - log_2(2r) = r - Theta(log r).

name: bent_quadratic_full_support_dual_form
statement: Take the bent quadratic q(z) = sum_{i=1}^t z_i z_{t+i} and v_z = (-1)^{q(z)} (tag 40). For a = (alpha,beta) in F_2^t x F_2^t the Walsh transform factors as (Hv)_a = prod_{i=1}^t sum_{u,w in F_2} (-1)^{uw + alpha_i u + beta_i w}, which lies in {+-2^t} (41). Hence the admissible full-dual form h_v = r^{-1}Hv has FULL support, the two-shadow graph is complete, and choosing h_v as the witness for the first pair of any perfect matching gives m = 1 batch (42), with nonzero coefficient at either endpoint so the exchange (35) is admissible.
notes: The bentness is what forces every Walsh coefficient to be nonzero, hence full support. This single-batch configuration is the engine of the O(m)-bootstrap refutation.

name: crosspolytope_selector_residual_lower_bound
statement: After the one-batch exchange on A_r, every signed-selector residual certificate has dimension d >= r - floor(log_2(2r)) (tag 43). Proof: let R be the residual span and pi the quotient map of rank q = r - d. Selector feasibility says every member of D~(A_r) has the same quotient image, up to sign, as one of the r members of the exchanged basis, so |pi(D~(A_r))| <= 2r (44). But (37) is an invertible linear image of the r-cube, and every rank-q linear image of a cube has at least 2^q distinct points (pick q input directions with independent images, fix the other signs, vary those q). Hence 2^{r-d} = 2^q <= 2r.
notes: For r = 2^{2t} the bound is r - (2t+1) while the number of batches remains ONE. The cube-image counting step (every rank-q linear image of a cube has >= 2^q points) is a reusable tool.

name: one_witness_per_batch_bootstrap_false
statement: The proposed inference 'one exchanged witness per batch implies residual rank O(m)' (tag 45) is FALSE, even for antipodal, spanning, fully closed REAL sign fibres. In the Walsh-Hadamard example the one selected dense equation certifies only an O(r^{-1/2}) Littlewood-Offord atom whereas the actual fibre density is 2r/2^r; the batching proof is intentionally allowed to leave almost all of that entropy defect unused, and the unselected full-dual rows retain r - O(log r) independent quotient complexity that triangular exchange does not see.
notes: S6's closing line: 'Pivot triangularity supplies basis admissibility and nothing stronger.' This is the sharpest known refutation of the dense-witness bootstrap and must be respected by any replacement argument.

name: bootstrap_repair_requirement
statement: A successful bootstrap would have to charge additional exchanges or residual directions to the REMAINING entropy defect after each batch, or prove a new quotient-class aggregation theorem. The refutation does not rule out deliberately choosing many SPARSE witnesses - the crosspolytope admits such choices with a number of batches of order r. It rules out entropy-efficient DENSE batching followed by an O(m) residual claim.
notes: Names the two surviving repair directions precisely, and preserves the sparse-witness escape hatch (which is what S9's bounded-congestion theorem exploits).

name: audit_verdict_thm1_thm2_pass
statement: S7 verdict: PASS, with two required wording/quantifier corrections. The weighted two-shadow compression theorem and the entropy-sharpened star-core rigidity theorem are correct; the triangular batching argument does give a product of conditional Littlewood-Offord factors and no independence of the selected constraint events is assumed. No dependency, exposure, Littlewood-Offord, or selector-rank counterexample was found.
notes: The two required corrections are (a) rewrite the reverse exposure with the disjoint U_s and explicit conditional expectation, (b) replace 'there is no cyclic wrap' by the finite-group one-point Littlewood-Offord theorem; plus the endpoint-threshold quantifier fix. This is an audit by a second agent reading the same project, NOT an independent re-derivation from primary sources.

name: disjoint_Us_structural_facts
statement: Five exact facts about the batching. (1) The batches B_s partition the matching edges, so the V_s are disjoint. (2) Hence the U_s = E_s cap V_s are pairwise disjoint. (3) |U_s| >= a_s + 1 (tag 6): the witness edge contributes both endpoints and each of the other a_s - 1 edges in B_s contributes at least one distinct endpoint. (4) E_t cap U_s = empty for t < s (tag 7): had E_t met an endpoint of a still-present edge of B_s, that edge would have been removed at stage t. (5) E_s meets no endpoint belonging to a later batch, so after fixing coordinates outside the union of the U_s, the indicator of the s-th selected constraint is a function of X_{U_1},...,X_{U_s} only (tag 8).
notes: The proof uses U_s, NOT the larger V_s - S7 states this explicitly. These five facts are the exact structural content the harness re-verifies by brute force.

name: reverse_conditional_expectation_identity
statement: Put Z = X restricted to the complement of the union of the U_s, Y_s = X_{U_s}, I_s = 1{h_s.X in {+-1}}. The blocks Y_1,...,Y_m,Z are mutually independent and I_s is measurable w.r.t. sigma(Z,Y_1,...,Y_s). Choosing any a_s+1 active coordinates in U_s and conditioning additionally on the rest of U_s turns the selected equation into a nonzero (a_s+1)-term Rademacher sum required to hit two arbitrary targets, so E[I_s | Z=z, Y_1,...,Y_{s-1}] <= psi(a_s+1) uniformly (tag 9). Reversing the blocks gives E[prod_s I_s | Z=z] <= prod_s psi(a_s+1) (10), hence 2^{-ell} = Pr(X in S) <= Pr(all I_s = 1) <= prod_s psi(a_s+1) (11).
notes: The |U_s| > a_s+1 case is handled by conditioning on the extra active coordinates BEFORE applying the (a_s+1)-term bound and averaging afterwards. S7: 'It does not assert that the events I_s = 1 are independent.'

name: two_target_three_quarter_bound
statement: After fixing all parameters outside a selected active set of size u, the event is sum_{i=1}^u c_i*eps_i in {b-1, b+1} with all c_i nonzero and b arbitrary (tag 12). For any two active coordinates, condition on the other u-2 signs: the four sums +-c_1 +- c_2 cannot all lie in a fixed two-point set when c_1,c_2 are nonzero. They have fewer than three distinct elements only if c_1 = +-c_2, in which case they are 0, 2c_1, -2c_1 up to translation - still three distinct values over R and over F_p with odd p > 2. Hence at most three of the four assignments work and the probability is <= 3/4 (13).
notes: Target-uniform and valid in every odd characteristic. This is the u = 2 branch of psi and the only branch that survives when u is small.

name: finite_group_one_point_LO
statement: Over R, sup_y Pr(sum_{i=1}^u c_i*eps_i = y) <= 2^{-u}*C(u, floor(u/2)) (tag 14). Over F_p the same inequality holds for nonzero coefficients when u < p - the finite-group Littlewood-Offord theorem in the no-wrap range (the F_p specialization of the optimal group inequality of Juskevicius-Semetulskis). In the application u <= r < p (15). Since p is odd the two targets b-1, b+1 are distinct, so applying (14) to each and taking a union bound gives <= 2^{1-u}*C(u, floor(u/2)) (16).
notes: [EXTRACTION-UNCERTAIN] the surname prints as 'JuskeviIius' in the text extraction; it is almost certainly Juskevicius (Juskevicius-Semetulskis). The hypothesis 'every nonzero coefficient has order p > u' is what licenses the central-binomial value.

name: no_cyclic_wrap_wording_is_not_a_proof
statement: The sentence 'the finite-field statement is valid because u < p, so there is no cyclic wrap' is NOT by itself a proof for arbitrary coefficients in F_p: arbitrary field coefficients can wrap numerically. What is true is that the optimal finite-group concentration theorem attains the central-binomial value when every nonzero coefficient has order p > u.
source: dossier pp.132-133 (S7 lines 184-185); correction 2 at p.138 (S7 line 414)
notes: A wording defect with real content: any future write-up must cite the finite-group theorem rather than argue by absence of wrap.

name: C0_equals_9_sharpening
statement: The endpoints of a maximum matching form a vertex cover of the two-shadow graph (a maximum matching is maximal), so |C| = 2N <= 9*4^ell (tag 22), and no support E_a can contain two vertices outside C since that pair would be an uncovered two-shadow edge. This proves Theorem 1 with the stronger admissible numerical choice C_0 = 9 (hence certainly with C_0 = 32).
notes: Use C_0 = 9 in any downstream computation; S6's C_0 = 32 is the safe-but-loose value. The N = 0 case must be separated before invoking the weighted sum (20).

name: thm2_edge_cases_and_antipodality
statement: Theorem 2 audit: correct, with edge cases to be stated. If C = empty then a noncoordinate row of support >= 2 would create a two-shadow edge and a nonempty matching, so no such core-only row exists. Discarded coordinate rows assign to themselves with zero residual. For a full-closed fibre, taking the rows to be its entire projective full dual makes their compatibility set exactly S; adding the input basis rows costs zero residual rank, and optimizing over coordinate bases gives the d_cb bound. Antipodality is harmless and in fact AUTOMATIC for a nonempty compatibility set defined by homogeneous two-sided constraints h_a.x in {+-1}. Final: d(H) <= |C| + |N_0| <= 9*4^ell + ell (28).
notes: No additional closure hypothesis is used inside the fixed-basis argument; full closure enters only when reinterpreting d(H) as d_cb over the whole full dual.

name: endpoint_arithmetic_o1_verification
statement: Under k = O(n/log n), ell -> infinity and 4^ell = o(ell log n) (tag 30): since r,j <= k one has n - r = n(1-o(1)) and j*log r + r + n = O(n) (31); (4^ell + ell)*k / ((n-r)*ell) = O(4^ell/(ell log n) + 1/log n) = o(1) (32); (j*log r + r + n)/((n-r)*ell) = O(1/ell) = o(1) (33). Hence the component exponent equals -(1-o(1))*(n-r)*ell (34).
notes: This is the arithmetic a transfer-lane argument must reuse when substituting a different coefficient for d_cb; note the coefficient enters multiplied by k and divided by (n-r)*ell.

name: six_required_corrections
statement: S7's exact correction list for the global bridge report: (1) replace the reverse-exposure paragraph of Theorem 1 by the U_s / conditional-expectation equations (5)-(11); (2) replace the no-cyclic-wrap sentence by the finite-group one-point Littlewood-Offord lemma plus the two-target union bound; (3) state that when |U_s| > a_s+1 the extra active coordinates are conditioned before applying the (a_s+1)-term bound; (4) separate the trivial N = 0 case before the weighted sum; (5) in Theorem 2 state how core-only rows are assigned, including the C = empty edge case; (6) qualify the lower-threshold conclusion as pointwise under (35) or as an infinite-subsequence conclusion.
notes: S7's closing sentence: with these corrections Theorems 1-2 and the controlled endpoint range are rigorous, but 'They remain exponential in ell and therefore do not close the high-corank connector-rigidity problem identified elsewhere in the report.'

name: harness_global_exponential_audit_checks
statement: The adversarial checker global_exponential_audit_checks.py (path /workspace/scratch/682eb2738f23/) uses exact integer/Fraction arithmetic to search for counterexamples to the triangular batching/exposure inequality and to the finite-field two-target Littlewood-Offord quantifiers. It implements psi(u) = min(3/4, 2*C(u,floor(u/2))/2^u), an exact maximum matching by memoized DP over vertex masks, a canonical greedy batching, exact rational rank, and full sign-cube enumeration.
source: dossier pp.139-144 (S8 lines 1-271); described at p.135 (S7 lines 306-311)
notes: S8 docstring: 'The searches are not used as proofs. They are exact counterexample searches.' Reproduction command: python3 global_exponential_audit_checks.py.

name: numeric_finite_field_lo_pass
statement: Checker output line: FINITE_FIELD_LO PASS coefficient_multisets=4370 u=2..8 primes<=13,p>u. The search ranges over u = 2..8, primes p in {3,5,7,11,13} with p > u, and all coefficient multisets in {1,...,(p-1)/2} of size u (exhaustive because sign changes and permutations preserve the distribution). For each it forms the exact frequency table of sum a_i*x_i mod p over all 2^u sign patterns, takes worst = max over centers of freq[(center-1) mod p] + freq[(center+1) mod p], and asserts worst <= min(3*2^u//4, 2*C(u,floor(u/2))).
source: dossier p.144 (S8 lines 241-260); output at p.135 (S8 line 330 / S7 line 313)
notes: FINITE WINDOW ONLY: u <= 8, p <= 13. It is evidence for psi in odd characteristic, not a proof; the proof is the finite-group Littlewood-Offord theorem. 4370 is the exact number of coefficient classes checked.

name: numeric_batching_pass
statement: Checker output line: BATCHING PASS exhaustive_systems=14592 random_systems=5000. Exhaustive part: every system of up to three normalized ternary rows in rank four and every system of up to two such rows in rank five (14,592 systems), where a normalized ternary row has entries in {-1,0,1}, support at least two, and first nonzero entry +1. Random part: 5,000 seeded systems (random.Random(20260815)) in ranks five through nine, with up to seven rows and coefficients in {+-1,+-2}.
source: dossier pp.143-144 (S8 lines 213-238); output at p.135 (S8 line 331 / S7 lines 314-315)
notes: FINITE WINDOW ONLY: ranks 4-5 exhaustively over ternary rows, ranks 5-9 by a seeded random sample. No claim of exhaustiveness beyond that; the random half is a sample, not a certificate over its range.

name: harness_stagewise_and_conditional_checks
statement: For every system the harness reconstructs a maximum matching, the batches and the actual U_s, then asserts: |U_s| >= |B_s| + 1; the U_s are pairwise disjoint; supp(E_t) cap U_s = empty for t < s; original_count <= selected_count; the global bound selected_count/2^r <= prod_s psi(|B_s|+1); the same product bound CONDITIONAL on EVERY assignment outside the union of the U_s; and every stagewise inequality count/2^{|U_s|} <= psi(|B_s|+1) for every assignment of the earlier U_t and of all other fixed coordinates.
notes: The conditional versions are the load-bearing checks: they test the reverse-exposure inequality pointwise in the conditioning, which is exactly the quantifier S7 required be made explicit.

name: harness_theorem2_selector_check
statement: On every nonempty compatibility set the harness takes C = the matching endpoints, computes the free / never-free partition of the outside coordinates (j is free iff some realized core pattern admits both signs of x_j among accepted points), asserts the deterministic cardinality inequality 2^{|N_0|} * |S| <= 2^r (equivalently |N_0| <= ell), builds the Theorem-2 selectors (signed coefficient for free j, +1 for never-free j, a core coordinate for core-only rows), and asserts the exact rational bound rank(residuals) <= |C| + |N_0|.
notes: 2^{|N_0|}*|S| <= 2^r is the exact CARDINALITY form of the entropy step (23), since |S| = 2^{r-ell}; useful as a cheap deterministic surrogate when auditing new families. Residual rank is computed in exact Fraction arithmetic.

name: harness_canonical_greedy_batching_scope
statement: The harness's make_batches implements ONE canonical allowed greedy batching (docstring: 'One canonical allowed greedy batching'): it always takes the lowest-index still-present matching pair and the lowest-index row containing it as witness. It does not enumerate all admissible greedy orders, witness choices, or maximum matchings.
notes: Scope caveat that matters when quoting BATCHING PASS: the checks certify the inequalities for that batching, which is enough for Theorem 1 (it needs only one displayed certificate) but is not a search over batchings - relevant if one later wants to MINIMIZE congestion kappa, which does quantify over batchings.

name: harness_evidence_scope_caveat
statement: S7 on its own searches: 'These searches are corroboration, not a replacement for Sections 2-5.' The finite-window results (u <= 8, p <= 13; ranks 4-5 exhaustive over ternary rows; ranks 5-9 sampled) may not be cited as proof of Theorems 1-2 or of psi in odd characteristic.
notes: Honesty boundary between the finite certificates and the analytic proof; keep it attached whenever the PASS counts are quoted.

name: bounded_congestion_verdict_constants
statement: S9 verdict. There is a rigorous linear-in-defect theorem for the part of the high-corank problem in which the weighted two-shadow batching has bounded entropy-normalized exposure congestion kappa. It is conditional, works on affine boundary fibres, uses the conditional defect that the dense-witness exchange leaves unused, and controls ALL unselected rows. In the original junction basis the constant is 2*kappa+1. If selected witnesses have private support at most s then kappa <= (s-1)/beta with beta = log_2(4/3), giving new quotient residual rank <= (1 + 2(s-1)/beta)*L (tag 1); insisting on the triangularly exchanged witness basis raises the constant by only beta^{-1}, to (1 + (2s-1)/beta)*L (tag 2).
notes: S9: 'This is a genuine residual-compression result, not the false inference that one residual direction is enough per selected witness.' Conditional on bounded kappa, which is precisely what the residual class (congestion >~ log n in every useful basis) denies.

name: rooted_setup_S9
statement: K = R, or K = F_p with odd p > q. (W,Q) is a sign basis on a finite support A with private part Q = (Q_1,...,Q_q). Set B = span_K W, R_< subset B, and L = q - H(Q|W) (tag 3). Private forms are Y_a = u_a(W) + h_a(Q) with Y_a(A) subset {+-1} (4), and E_a = supp h_a. Boundary-only forms are passed to the parent. Singleton private supports are RETAINED but do not create two-shadow edges. The private two-shadow graph has edge ij whenever some E_a contains both i and j.
notes: The retention of singleton private supports is what lets the NAE-star counterexample have an EMPTY two-shadow graph while still having forms to select - do not silently discard them.

name: bounded_congestion_residual_compression_S9_thm1
statement: S9 Theorem 1. In the rooted setup, a coordinate-selector certificate R exists with dim((R+B)/B) <= (2*kappa+1)*L (tag 7), where kappa is the congestion of any one certified batching. No full-closure and no antipodality hypothesis is needed. Proof: L = E_w[q - log_2|A_w|] (8); pick w_0 with q - log_2|A_{w_0}| <= L so the affine compatibility set has density >= 2^{-L}; reverse exposure gives 2^{-L} <= prod psi(a_s+1), i.e. sum_s c_s <= L (10); then N = sum a_s <= kappa*sum c_s <= kappa*L (11), |C| = 2N <= 2*kappa*L (12); free/never-free gives lambda_a = +-1 (13) and |N_0| <= L (15); all residual private projections lie in P_0 = span Q_{C union N_0} with dim P_0 <= (2kappa+1)L (16); project along B.
notes: S9 marks the exact step (line 163-164): 'This is precisely where the conditional entropy defect, rather than an unconditional block defect, is used.' The edge case C = empty is harmless: a core-only row is then boundary-only and already passed to the parent. Not separately audited by S7 (which covers S6 only).

name: unrooted_bounded_support_linear_rank_bound
statement: For an unrooted homogeneous fibre B = 0, so S9 Theorem 1 is already a true residual rank bound: if selected witness private support is at most s then d(H) <= (1 + 2(s-1)/beta)*ell (tag 17), beta = log_2(4/3).
notes: S9: 'Unlike the invalid one-direction-per-batch bootstrap, this proof controls every unselected row through the matching vertex cover and the free/never-free entropy dichotomy.' This is a genuine LINEAR-in-defect theorem, but only under bounded witness support.

name: witness_exchange_costs_L_over_beta
statement: With m batches, choosing one pivot p_s per witness pair and replacing Q_{p_s} by the sign-valued witness Y_s, the pivot matrix is triangular modulo B with nonzero diagonal, so (W, Y_1,...,Y_m, Q_j for j not a pivot) (tag 18) is an admissible sign basis. For each fixed boundary value it is an invertible change of private coordinates, hence preserves H(Q|W) and L. From sum c_s <= L and c_s >= beta, m <= L/beta (19). Keeping old selectors and adding the exchange discrepancies e_s = Q_{p_s} - Y_s (20) gives exchanged-basis quotient residual rank <= (2kappa+1)L + m <= (2kappa+1+beta^{-1})L (21).
notes: beta^{-1} = 1/log_2(4/3) = 2.40942 - the same constant as the NAE three-circuit floor, appearing here as the price of the exchange. The invariance of L under the exchange is what makes the charge additive rather than multiplicative.

name: crosspolytope_kappa_r_over_log_r
statement: The crosspolytope (Walsh-Hadamard) counterexample is consistent with S9 Theorem 1: its one dense batch has a_1 asymptotic to r and c_1 asymptotic to log r, so kappa is asymptotic to r/log r - unbounded. The (2kappa+1)L bound is therefore vacuous there, which is exactly why it does not contradict the r - O(log r) residual-rank lower bound.
notes: The reconciliation that makes bounded congestion the RIGHT hypothesis: the known counterexample lives exactly at unbounded kappa. Any attempt to remove the kappa hypothesis must explain this family.

name: lemma2_connector_factorization
statement: Write the chosen residual generators uniquely as r_a = b_a + p_a with b_a in B and p_a in P_0 (tag 22). Let F be the free coefficient space on the generators and define P: F -> P_0, e_a -> p_a, and Bbar: F -> B/R_<, e_a -> b_a + R_< (23). The following are EQUIVALENT: (1) R cap B subset R_<; (2) ker P subset ker Bbar; (3) there is a linear T: im P -> B/R_< with Bbar = T o P. Under them, dim((R+R_<)/R_<) = dim((R+B)/B) <= (2kappa+1)L (24).
notes: Proof: sum lambda_a r_a lies in B exactly when P*lambda = 0, and its boundary class mod R_< is Bbar*lambda (1 iff 2); the quotient factorization lemma gives (2 iff 3); the projection of (R+R_<)/R_< onto (R+B)/B is surjective with zero kernel under condition 1, hence an isomorphism. THIS IS THE EXACT ABSORPTION CRITERION - it converts an existential clause of target (3) into a checkable kernel containment.

name: exchanged_basis_augmented_kernel_test
statement: For the exchanged basis, apply Lemma 2 to the AUGMENTED residual list {r_a} union {e_s}. This is a convenient sufficient test and can be STRONGER THAN NECESSARY, because the actual transformed residuals may use only particular combinations of the e_s. If the augmented kernel condition holds, (21) becomes the full rooted bound dim((R+R_<)/R_<) <= (2kappa+1+beta^{-1})*L with R cap B subset R_< (tag 25).
notes: The over-strength of the augmented test is a live slack: a block failing it may still absorb. Relevant to anyone hunting counterexamples - failing the augmented test is not a counterexample to absorption.

name: absorption_structural_certificates
statement: Three small certificates for ker P subset ker Bbar. (a) PRIVATE ANCHORS: if the matrix of private residual projections has full column rank then ker P = 0; a triangular system of distinct private anchors proves this immediately. (b) GRAPHIC/NETWORK CYCLIC BLOCKS: if P is a scaled oriented incidence matrix then ker P is generated by fundamental cycles, so it suffices to verify that the signed boundary trace around each fundamental cycle lies in R_<; equivalently, modulo R_<, the connector labels are differences of vertex potentials. (c) BOUNDED DEPENDENCY BASIS: any displayed basis of ker P is a finite certificate - check its boundary trace under Bbar; this is the appropriate exact-arithmetic test for a finite normal-form block.
notes: For a bounded-support high-corank cyclic block, bounded congestion gives the linear rank charge while cycle closure gives absorption - the two hypotheses are independent and both needed. (b) is the concrete cohomological-flavoured test: connector labels must be exact as a potential difference mod R_<.

name: common_linear_lift_is_condition_3
statement: The 'common-linear-lift' language of recursive_paired_block_tree_entropy.md is PRECISELY condition 3 of Lemma 2: the existence of a linear T: im P -> B/R_< with Bbar = T o P.
notes: Load-bearing for the campaign: recursive_paired_block_tree_entropy.md is cited but NOT reproduced in the dossier and is absent from every machine this campaign controls, so this sentence plus S14's condition (14) is the entire surviving specification of its interface. S9 adds: Lemma 2 makes clear both what a witness-basis exchange must preserve and why pivot triangularity alone is insufficient.

name: nae_star_exact_counterexample
statement: Real sign coordinates W = (x_1,z_1,x_2,z_2,x_3,z_3), Q = (q) (tag 26), with three NAE forms Y_i = x_i + z_i + q, i = 1,2,3 (27), and A = {(W,q) in {+-1}^7 : Y_i in {+-1} for i = 1,2,3} (28). For fixed q each pair has exactly three allowed values, so |A| = 2*3^3 = 54 (29). The fibre is antipodal, spanning and fully closed. Both values of q occur at a fixed W exactly when all three pairs are opposite, mass 2*2^3/(2*3^3) = 8/27; otherwise q is determined. Hence H(q|W) = 8/27 and L = 19/27 (30). Every private support is the singleton {q}, private incidence degree is three, and the two-shadow graph is EMPTY. Selecting q for each Y_i gives residuals x_i+z_i: quotient residual rank mod B is ZERO while the unpaid boundary residual rank is THREE.
notes: Spanning is proved by fixing q = 1 and all pairs but one: the three allowed values of that pair are affinely spanning, forcing the two coefficients of any vanishing form to vanish, after which the coefficient of q vanishes. Full closure: the three displayed full-dual forms already cut out (28). The point: (7) can be EXTREMELY strong (bound 0) while absorption completely fails.

name: nae_star_full_dual_classification
statement: On the slice q = 1 the domain is the product of three copies of T = {(1,-1),(-1,1),(-1,-1)} (tag 31). If a linear sign-valued form has nonconstant contributions from two pair blocks, the sum of their two ranges has at least three real values, impossible for a {+-1}-valued form; so it uses at most one pair. Solving the three values on one NAE triple shows the projective possibilities are exactly q, x_i, z_i, Y_i (32). Consequently a sign basis retaining the incoming boundary W must take its one private member to be either q or one Y_j, up to sign.
notes: A complete classification of the full dual - this is what makes the impossibility argument exhaustive over boundary-preserving bases rather than merely over the obvious ones.

name: nae_star_no_boundary_preserving_repair
statement: No boundary-preserving admissible sign basis repairs the NAE-star absorption failure. Whatever the basis takes as its single private member (q, or one Y_j, up to sign), two of the three forms - call them Y_i, Y_k - remain, and for EVERY signed selector choice their residuals are linearly independent. Their span therefore has dimension at least 2 while its private projection has dimension at most 1, so the span contains a nonzero pure-boundary vector. With R_< = 0, connector absorption is impossible.
notes: Proof of the independence: the residual Y_i -/+ g retains at least one of the two boundary coordinates x_i, z_i private to that row; a residual from Y_k meets at most one of x_i, z_i, since a basis selector has at most one such boundary coordinate and the sole nonboundary basis form is supported on the j-th pair; if the two were proportional, the first would have to cancel one of its own pair coordinates by selecting it and would then have no support on x_k, z_k, while the second necessarily retains one - contradiction. Quantifier is over ALL boundary-preserving admissible sign bases AND all signed selector choices. R_< = 0 is essential: the leak is fatal only when ancestors have paid nothing.

name: nae_star_leak_to_defect_ratios
statement: Arithmetic consequences of the NAE-star numbers: with L = 19/27, the naive selection's unpaid boundary leak rank 3 gives leak/L = 81/19 = 4.263..., and the forced minimum of one pure-boundary leak direction gives leak/L >= 27/19 = 1.421.... Hence any LEAK-charging inequality of the form leak <= C''*L needs C'' >= 27/19 on this family, and >= 81/19 if the naive selection must also be covered.
notes: DERIVED BY THE DIGESTER from the source's exact numbers (L = 19/27 at tag 30, leak rank 3 at line 417-418, forced leak >= 1 at lines 455-457). These ratios are NOT printed in S9. They constrain a leak-charging route, not target (3) itself, which counts leak inside dim((R+R_<)/R_<).

name: nae_star_logical_role
statement: S9 on the scope of its counterexample: 'This example is a low-rank star, not one of the final cyclic SCC survivors. Its role is logical: bounded private row support, bounded private incidence degree, conditional defect, and basis optimization do not imply connector absorption. A cycle-kernel/common-lift condition, or some stronger structural replacement for it, is indispensable.'
notes: Guards against two misreadings: (a) that the star is a counterexample to the conjecture (it is not - it is outside the residual class), and (b) that some milder hypothesis than a coherence/lift condition could be found.

name: absorption_hypothesis_is_necessary
statement: Connector absorption does not follow from bounded support, overlap, or incidence degree: a fully closed spanning antipodal affine star with private support ONE and private incidence degree THREE has no absorbing signed-selector certificate for ANY boundary-preserving admissible sign basis. Hence a connector compatibility hypothesis is mathematically necessary. The exact useful hypothesis is the kernel/factorization certificate: every linear dependency among the private projections of the chosen residuals must have boundary trace already in the ancestor residual space; under it, (1) - or (2) after exchange - gives the full rooted estimate (3).
notes: S9's headline negative result. It forecloses any proof of target (3) that hopes to derive clause (ii) from local sparsity/degree data alone.

name: s9_integration_four_step_recipe
statement: The valid replacement for the residual-compression step: (1) exhibit a maximum-matching batching with bounded kappa (bounded witness support, matching overlap, or two-shadow degree suffices); (2) use S9 Theorem 1 to charge the ENTIRE unselected residual quotient to the conditional defect L; (3) if the witness exchange is required, add its at most L/beta discrepancy directions; (4) verify the connector kernel on a dependency basis, preferably a fundamental-cycle basis in a network-type cyclic block. Under these explicit hypotheses the block satisfies the rooted linear estimate needed by the recursive telescope.
notes: S9: 'Without step 4, even support-one, degree-three fully closed fibres fail the absorption statement.' The recipe covers bounded-support cyclic blocks whose connector labels close on a fundamental-cycle basis - in particular scaled graphic or network residual systems with paid cycle sums.

name: s9_final_open_problem
statement: S9's closing statement of the gap, verbatim in substance: the remaining open problem is to DERIVE such coherence, or an alternative global aggregation mechanism, for the genuinely dense high-corank cyclic SCCs, rather than ASSUME it. The bounded-congestion theorem does not solve the remaining dense, noncoherent singleton-layer SCC.
source: dossier p.155 (S9 lines 481-483); scope note p.146 (S9 lines 53-56)
notes: Note the explicit alternative offered by the source: an ALTERNATIVE GLOBAL AGGREGATION MECHANISM is an acceptable substitute for deriving coherence. That is the widest opening in the whole pp.113-155 range.

name: rooted_nae_cycle_fibre_An
statement: For n >= 4, indices in Z/nZ: A_n = {(a,b_1,...,b_n) in {+-1}^{n+1} : a+b_i+b_{i+1} in {+-1} for every i}. On the half a=1 the condition excludes exactly the local pattern b_i=b_{i+1}=1, so S={i : b_i=1} is an independent (stable) set of the cycle C_n and every independent set occurs; the half a=-1 is its antipode. a is the 'root'/homogenizer coordinate.
notes: This single family is the object of S10-S14. n >= 4 is used so that the cliques of C_n are exactly the empty set, the vertices and the edges.

name: dgeo_dcb_for_this_source_range
statement: d_geo(A) = minimum dimension of a real residual subspace R inducing no more signed projective classes on the full dual than the ambient rank r permits (a 'feasible geometric quotient' has at most r signed classes, counting one zero class if it occurs). d_cb(A) = minimum, over coordinate bases drawn from the full dual together with signed selectors, of dim of the common residual space. Every selector certificate is in particular a feasible geometric quotient, hence d_geo(A) <= d_cb(A) always.
notes: Anchor definition for the whole S10-S14 range; d_geo <= d_cb is the direction used to turn the mod-2 lower bound into a lower bound on d_cb.

name: rooted_nae_cycle_full_dual_Dn
statement: The projective full dual of A_n is exactly D_n = {A, B_i, C_i : i in Z/nZ} with A=e_0, B_i=e_i, C_i=e_0+e_i+e_{i+1}. Proof: normalize a sign-valued affine form on the positive half to value -1 at the empty independent set; its values on the singletons force every singleton increment to be 0 or 2, so the form is -1+2|S cap K| for a vertex set K; it is sign-valued on every independent set iff K is a clique; for n>=4 the cliques of C_n are the empty clique, the vertices and the edges. The edge forms cut out the defining condition, so the fibre is FULL CLOSED. Rank r = n+1 (witnessed by the empty and the n singleton independent sets).
source: dossier p.158 (S10 lines 102-131, (11)-(13); r=n+1 at line 99)
notes: Full closure matters: the counterexample family is not a nonspanning or non-closed artefact. Repeated verbatim at S12 (3) p.174 and S14 (5) p.185.

name: rooted_nae_cycle_cardinality_and_defect
statement: |A_n| = 2*I(C_n) = 2*(F_{n-1}+F_{n+1}) = 2*L_n (L_n the n-th Lucas number); rank r = n+1; density defect ell(A_n) = n - log_2 L_n. Explicit Lucas values used: (L_4,...,L_13) = (7,11,18,29,47,76,123,199,322,521); L_42 = 599074578. For even n, L_n = phi^n + phi^{-n} > phi^n, so ell(A_n) < n(1 - log_2 phi).
notes: L_42 = 599074578 re-derived independently by this digester from the Lucas recurrence: MATCHES. ell(A_42) = 42 - log_2(599074578) = 12.8418396275, matching S11's printed digits exactly.

name: cycle_two_shadow_quotient_lemma_2_1
statement: (Lemma 2.1, cycle two-shadow quotient.) Let S_n = {0} u {u_i : 1<=i<=n} u {u_i+u_{i+1} : 1<=i<=n} in F_2^n, u_i the standard basis, indices cyclic. For EVERY subspace W <= F_2^n of dimension w, the number of occupied cosets obeys |S_n/W| >= 2n+1-3w. Proof: pick Q subset [n], |Q|=n-w, whose singleton cosets are a basis of F_2^n/W; deleting the w vertices of [n]\Q from a cycle destroys at most 2w edges, so at least max{0,n-2w} edges have both endpoints in Q; their images are sums of two distinct basis vectors, mutually distinct and distinct from 0 and every singleton. Count 1+(n-w)+max{0,n-2w}; for w<=n/2 this is the bound, for w>=n/2 the first two terms already are.
notes: The coefficient 3 is EXACT: quotienting by <u_i> identifies the three pairs 0~u_i, u_{i-1}~u_{i-1}+u_i, u_{i+1}~u_i+u_{i+1}, and widely separated choices of i make the bound an equality (S10 (19), p.160). This is the whole source of the n/3 rate and of 'one residual direction pays three quotient mergers'.

name: saturated_lattice_mod2_transfer
statement: Transfer from real signed projective classes to a binary quotient. Given a real residual R of dim d, replace R by R_0 = span of (every f in D_n in the zero class) and (every f - sigma*g in R, sigma in {+-1}, witnessing a class equality). R_0 is rational, contained in R, of dim d_0 <= d, and induces exactly the same classes. Put Lambda = R_0 cap Z^{n+1}; it is saturated, hence a direct summand of Z^{n+1}, so its mod-2 reduction has dimension d_0. Signs die in characteristic two, so the real signed partition (zero class included) REFINES the coset partition mod Lambda-bar. All D_n vectors have odd weight; translating by A=e_0 lands in the even-weight space E with basis u_i=e_0+e_i, sending A->0, B_i->u_i, C_i->u_i+u_{i+1}. Set W = Lambda-bar cap E, dim W <= d_0 <= d.
source: dossier pp.160-161 (S10 lines 199-256, (20)-(24)), audited at pp.167-169 (S11 lines 30-107)
notes: No reduction-of-rank assumption is hidden: passing to the SATURATED lattice is precisely what stops a denominator divisible by 2 from invalidating the mod-2 argument (S10 lines 269-272, p.162). The zero class costs no lost +1 (S11 lines 104-106). Field-critical: the argument is R -> F_2 and uses sigma=+-1 |-> 1.

name: primitive_lattice_dimension_preservation
statement: (S11 audit of the transfer.) Lambda = R_0 cap Z^{n+1} is primitive: if k*z in Lambda with z in Z^{n+1}, k != 0, then k*z in R_0, hence z in R_0, so z in Lambda. Equivalently Z^{n+1}/Lambda is torsion-free and Lambda extends to an integer basis, so dim_{F_2} Lambda-bar = d_0 exactly. Consequently k_{D_n}(R_old) >= |S_n/W| >= 2n+1-3*dim W >= 2n+1-3d.
notes: This is the audit's fully-justified version of the chain; the audit's only requested change is to write d_0 <= d explicitly rather than silently reuse d.

name: signed_class_lower_bound_corollary_3_1
statement: (Corollary 3.1, eq (25).) For every real residual space R of dimension d, the number k_{D_n}(R) of signed projective classes on D_n (counting one zero class if it occurs) satisfies k_{D_n}(R) >= 2n+1-3d.
notes: Uniform in n, no computational input. This is the only lower-bound engine in the whole S10-S14 range.

name: dgeo_rooted_nae_cycle_exact
statement: (S10 eq (2).) For every n >= 4, d_geo(A_n) = ceil(n/3). Lower bound: a feasible geometric quotient has at most r = n+1 signed classes, so Corollary 3.1 forces n+1 >= 2n+1-3d, i.e. d >= ceil(n/3). Upper bound: choose an independent U in V(C_n) with |U| = ceil(n/3) and take R = span{L_u = A+B_u : u in U}; modulo R, adding or deleting a vertex of U from a clique does not change its signed class, so classes are indexed by cliques of C_n - U, which has n-|U| vertices, n-2|U| edges and no clique bigger than an edge: at most 1+(n-|U|)+(n-2|U|) = 2n+1-3|U| <= n+1 classes.
notes: Uniform in n with NO computational input (earlier support had been exact finite searches only). Independently re-verified here by exhaustive search over all residual spaces of dim <= ceil(n/3)-1 spanned by zero-class forms and signed differences, n=4..8: zero feasible quotients (see local_rerun_exhaustive_dgeo_minimality).

name: dcb_geq_dgeo_rooted_nae_cycle
statement: (S10 eq (30).) Since every selector certificate is in particular a feasible geometric quotient, d_cb(A_n) >= d_geo(A_n) = ceil(n/3).
notes: Matching upper bound d_cb <= ceil(n/3) is supplied independently by S12 and S14, closing d_cb = d_geo.

name: rooted_nae_full_dual_matroid_three_connected
statement: (Lemma 5.1.) For every n >= 4 the real projective matroid on D_n is three-connected. Proof: the n fundamental relations C_i - A - B_i - B_{i+1} = 0 give a dual representation (up to column signs) by t = sum_i e_i, p_i = e_i, q_i = e_i+e_{i+1} in R^n, of rank n. No loops, coloops or singleton one-separations. For a partition (X,Y) with |X|,|Y| >= 2 and t in X, set a = #{i : p_i in X}, b = #{i : q_i in X}; a case analysis on the pinned forest components of the X- and Y-edge systems gives (n-r(X))+(n-r(Y)) <= n-2, i.e. lambda(X) = r(X)+r(Y)-n >= 2. Duality preserves the connectivity function.
notes: This is what makes the counterexample fatal to the three-connected shortcut: the obstruction is NOT produced by a hidden 1- or 2-separation. [EXTRACTION-UNCERTAIN, harmless] the extraction prints 'qquad' without its backslash inside (32) and (34); spacing only, no mathematical content lost.

name: three_connectivity_endpoint_cases_b0_bn_over_R
statement: (S11 audit sec.3, the two endpoint cases done over the REALS.) With delta_X = n-r(X), delta_Y = n-r(Y), t in X: (b=0) if a<n then delta_X = n-a-1 and, since |X|>=2 gives a>=1 while the Y-system holds the full cycle plus at least one Y-pin so delta_Y = 0, the sum is <= n-2; if a=n then delta_X=0 and the unpinned full Y-cycle has defect 0 for odd n and 1 for even n. (b=n) if a=0 then delta_Y=0 and the full X-cycle has defect 0 for odd n, while for EVEN n its alternating null vector survives the total-sum equation so delta_X=1; if a>0 an X-pin kills the cycle nullspace so delta_X=0 and delta_Y=a <= n-2 by |Y|>=2.
notes: FIELD-SENSITIVE: the even-cycle alternating null vector is real and must not be discarded; the audit flags exactly this. S10's own text compresses these cases ('the full Y-cycle is killed by any Y-pin; with no pin it has dimension at most one'), which the audit expands.

name: singleton_connectivity_lambda_one
statement: (S11 audit completion.) Every displayed dual column is nonzero; deleting t or any q_i leaves all p_i and hence full rank; deleting p_i leaves p_j (j != i) together with q_i = p_i+p_{i+1}, so also full rank. Therefore every singleton has lambda({e}) = 1+n-n = 1, not zero. Combined with lambda(X) >= 2 for |X|,|Y| >= 2 this proves genuine 3-connectivity, including the smallest endpoint n=4.
notes: One of the two clarifications the audit asks to be made explicit; it changes no stated bound.

name: ceiling_rado_constant_one_claim
statement: DISPROVED. The three-connected strengthening 'q_ev(A) >= floor(log_2|A|), and hence d_cb(A) <= ceil(ell(A))' (S10 eq (1)) is FALSE, even for an infinite family of full-closed fibres whose projective full-dual matroids are genuinely three-connected. The rooted NAE cycles are the counterexamples.
source: dossier p.156 (S10 lines 5-14), verdict audited PASS at p.173 (S11 lines 303-309)
notes: CONDITION OF FAILURE: three-connectivity plus full closure are NOT enough to force constant one; the failure is extensive (deficit n/3+O(1) against defect (1-log_2 phi)n+o(1)), not a finite anomaly.

name: q_ev_floor_log_cardinality_rado_claim
statement: DISPROVED. By the Rado certificate lemma, a bound q_ev >= floor(log_2|A_n|) would imply the contradicted ceiling bound; therefore q_ev(A_n) < floor(log_2|A_n|) (S10 eq (41)) for every member of the subfamily n = 0 mod 6, n >= 42, DESPITE Lemma 5.1 (three-connectivity).
notes: CONDITION OF FAILURE: a maximal evaluation-row Rado argument cannot have the hoped-for constant one on three-connected blocks. The dossier does not restate the Rado certificate lemma itself in pp.156-200 (UNKNOWN in this range).

name: three_connected_block_ceiling_charging_shortcut
statement: DISPROVED (S10 sec.7). The proposed global shortcut -- 'decompose the full dual into three-connected matroid blocks, and charge every three-connected block with the ceiling estimate d_cb <= ceil(ell)' -- is ruled out: the rooted NAE cycles are ALREADY single three-connected blocks and the failure is extensive rather than an isolated finite anomaly (exact geometric deficit n/3+O(1) against density defect (1-log_2 phi)n+o(1)).
notes: CONDITION OF FAILURE: block decomposition into three-connected pieces gives no entropy payment. A block decomposition proof needs a genuine entropy loss INSIDE a three-connected cyclic block; it cannot declare every such block ceiling-rigid (S10 lines 64-67, p.157).

name: infinite_ceiling_counterexample_family
statement: For even n, L_n = phi^n + phi^{-n} > phi^n, hence ell(A_n) = n - log_2 L_n < n(1-log_2 phi). With delta = 1/3 - (1-log_2 phi) = 0.0275752469..., if n = 0 mod 6 and n >= 42 then delta*n > 1, so ell(A_n) < n/3 - 1 and ceil(ell(A_n)) <= n/3 - 1 < n/3 = d_geo(A_n) <= d_cb(A_n). Hence (S10 eq (5)) d_cb(A_n) >= n/3 > ceil(ell(A_n)) for every such n.
source: dossier pp.165-166 (S10 lines 420-451), audited p.173 (S11 lines 266-301)
notes: First member n=42: L_42 = 599074578, ell(A_42) = 12.8418396275..., d_geo(A_42) = 14; delta*42 = 1.15816037248... > 1. All four numbers independently re-derived here and matching (delta*42 agrees to 10 of the 11 printed digits; last digit is rounding).

name: n13_ceiling_counterexample
statement: Exact finite counterexample at n=13: d_cb(A_13) >= d_geo(A_13) = 5 while L_13 = 521 and ell(A_13) = 13 - log_2 521 = 3.9748604377..., so ceil(ell(A_13)) = 4 < 5. Audit's explicit certificate: U = {1,3,5,8,11} (one-based cyclic) is independent of size five; C_13 - U has 8 vertices and 3 edges so the certificate has at most 1+8+3 = 12 <= 14 = r classes; conversely a residual space of dimension four would have at least 2*13+1-3*4 = 15 > 14 classes.
notes: Re-verified here: gaps of U are 2,2,3,3,3 (sum 13, all >= 2 so independent); C_13-U = {2,4,6,7,9,10,12,13} with edges 6-7, 9-10, 12-13, exactly 3. This is a FINITE certificate about n=13, not an asymptotic claim.

name: dgeo_over_ell_ratio_limit
statement: (S10 eq (6).) d_geo(A_n)/ell(A_n) -> 1/(3(1-log_2 phi)) = 1.090186..., phi = (1+sqrt5)/2. Consequently the rooted NAE cycles do NOT disprove an absolute linear theorem d_cb = O(ell); what they show is that neither three-connectivity nor a maximal evaluation-row Rado argument can have the previously hoped-for constant one.
notes: Re-derived here as 1.090186485. CAUTION for downstream use: this 1.09 is the ROOTED-NAE-CYCLE family's ratio only; it is NOT the campaign's constant floor. Within pp.156-200 the largest forced constant is C_int = 2.949539... (S14, intervals uniform over descendant attachments).

name: entropy_payment_inside_a_three_connected_cyclic_block
statement: S10 sec.7's statement of what remains: one residual direction can account for THREE quotient mergers in this family (exactly as in the tightness example (19) of Lemma 2.1), and those directions must be paid at positive entropy cost throughout the cyclic block. Merely invoking three-connectivity or maximal Rado transversality cannot supply that payment. The family remains compatible with a constant-factor conditional-counting or activation theorem, so it is NOT a counterexample to the desired global O(ell) conclusion.
notes: This is what S12/S14 then supply FOR THIS FAMILY (activation cells). It is exactly the piece that remains unsupplied for dense connector-incoherent cores -- the campaign's single hardest open piece.

name: s11_audit_verdict_pass_two_clarifications
statement: Independent audit of rigidity_attack_report.md: VERDICT PASS. The main theorem d_geo(A_n) = ceil(n/3) (n>=4) is correct, the full-dual real matroid is three-connected, the n=13 example is a valid ceiling counterexample, and every n = 0 mod 6, n >= 42 belongs to the asserted infinite family. No substantive gap was found in the mod-2 transfer, the upper certificate, or the endpoint connectivity cases. Two sentences should be made explicit: (1) after rationalizing the residual space, denote its dimension d_0 <= d rather than silently reusing d; (2) after proving lambda(X) >= 2 for |X|,|Y| >= 2, separately note that every displayed dual column is a nonloop and noncoloop, disposing of singleton one-separations. Neither point changes any stated bound.
source: dossier p.167 (S11 lines 3-27), final assessment p.173 (S11 lines 303-309)
notes: NOT independent evidence in the campaign's sense: S11 audits S10 by reading it. It IS an independent re-derivation of the endpoint connectivity cases and of the n=13 arithmetic.

name: independent_dominating_set_gap_table_all_residues
statement: For every n >= 4 an independent set U of C_n of size ceil(n/3) exists with all cyclic gaps of length 2 or 3: n = 3k -> |U| = k, gaps 3,...,3; n = 3k+1 -> |U| = k+1, gaps 2,2,3,...,3; n = 3k+2 -> |U| = k+1, gaps 2,3,...,3. The residuals L_u = A+B_u = e_0+e_u are linearly independent because the e_u coordinate occurs only in L_u. With F_empty = -A, F_{i} = B_i, F_{i,i+1} = C_i one has F_{u} - F_empty = L_u and F_{u,v} - F_{v} = L_u, so every clique form is congruent mod span{L_u} to the form obtained by deleting its U-vertices. Deleting an independent U removes exactly 2|U| cycle edges.
source: dossier pp.169-170 (S11 lines 110-166), same table at p.175 (S12 eq (5), lines 63-72)
notes: Proves feasibility in ALL THREE congruence classes mod 3, not only 3 | n. All gaps >= 2 (independence) AND <= 3 (domination) are both load-bearing -- see coverage_check_enforces_dominating_gaps.

name: dcb_equals_dgeo_rooted_nae_cycle
statement: (S12 eq (1).) For the rooted NAE cycle fibre, for every n >= 4: d_cb(A_n) = d_geo(A_n) = ceil(n/3). The geometric lower bound of S10 is ATTAINED by an actual coordinate-basis selector certificate, so the family is a solved high-corank cyclic class.
source: dossier p.174 (S12 lines 16-18), independently re-proved with a different basis at p.184/p.189 (S14 (1),(21))
notes: Two DIFFERENT explicit bases prove the upper bound (S12 sec.3 and S14 (14)); see s12_and_s14_selector_bases_differ.

name: explicit_selector_basis_gapwise_S12
statement: Selector basis (S12 sec.3). Orient the cycle; for a length-two gap u-v-u' select B_v, C_v; for a length-three gap u-v-w-u' select B_v, C_v, C_w. Let B_U = {A} together with all gap-selected forms; every gap of length g contributes g forms so |B_U| = 1 + sum_gaps g = n+1 = r. Independence: in a putative dependence the coordinate B_{u'} occurs in exactly one selected form of the preceding gap (its final C-form), so that coefficient vanishes; moving backwards through the gap kills the rest, then A. Representatives modulo R = span{L_u}: A and the selected forms represent themselves; B_u = -A for u in U; in a length-three gap B_w = C_w (C_w-B_w = L_{u'}); the edge form leaving u in U obeys C_u = B_v (C_u-B_v = L_u). These cases exhaust D_n, so d_cb(A_n) <= dim R = ceil(n/3).
notes: Explains the three-at-a-time quotient mergers of the binary lower bound: a length-three gap is paid by ONE residual direction while retaining a genuine coordinate-basis transversal. This is the basis implemented by the S13 checker.

name: gap_factorization_f2_f3
statement: (S12 (12)-(13).) Once the states at U are prescribed, independent-set choices factor over the gaps. For a length-two gap with endpoint states s,t in {0,1}: f_2(s,t) = 2 if s=t=0, else 1; and f_2(s,t) <= 2^{1-(s+t)/2}. For a length-three gap (its two interior vertices form an edge): f_3(s,t) = 3 if s+t=0, 2 if s+t=1, 1 if s+t=2; and f_3(s,t) <= 2^{2-(s+t)/2}.
notes: Both exponent bounds are tight only at their extreme states (f_2 at s=t=0 and at s+t=2). Multiplying over the cyclic gaps works because each selected u is an endpoint exactly TWICE, so sum of (s+t)/2 over gaps = |z|, and sum of (g-1) over gaps = n-d.

name: activation_cell_inequality_cycle_S12
statement: (S12 eq (2)/(14).) For u in U put Z_u = 1{L_u != 0}; on the half a=1 this is 1{u in S} for the corresponding independent set S, and the half a=-1 is antipodal with the same activation vector. Then for every z in {0,1}^U the number of independent sets with S cap U = z is at most 2^{n-d-|z|}, and restoring the antipodal half gives |A_{n,z}| <= 2^{n+1-d-|z|} = 2^{r-d-|z|}, with r = n+1 and d = ceil(n/3).
notes: This is the UNCONDITIONAL (root-marginal) form. S14 (24) upgrades it to a TARGET-UNIFORM form conditional on an arbitrary incoming boundary value w -- that stronger version is the one the connector programme needs.

name: aggregate_three_quarters_power_density
statement: (S12 eq (15).) Summing the activation-cell bound over z gives |A_n|/2^{n+1} <= (3/4)^d, hence d <= ell(A_n)/log_2(4/3). The exact Lucas-number density is stronger asymptotically, but (15) is the TENSOR-STABLE bound needed by the activation programme.
notes: 1/log_2(4/3) = 2.409420840... . Measured here: the bound is LOOSE by a factor 2-5 against the exact Lucas density (n=16: L_n/2^n = 0.0337 vs (3/4)^6 = 0.1780). So it never pins d; see activation_cell_bound_is_not_tight_on_the_cycle.

name: connector_transversality_root_boundary_S12
statement: (S12 sec.5.) Treat A = e_0 as the incoming boundary coordinate and the B_i = e_i as private. Projection of R = span{L_u} to the private space sends L_u |-> B_u and is injective, hence R cap span{A} = {0} (eq (16)). Thus the selector space creates NO new boundary-only residual direction and the connector-absorption clause holds for every ancestor residual space. Conditioning on the root sign leaves a uniform independent-set fibre, so L_{B|A} = n - H(B|A) = n - log_2 L_n = ell(A_n) (eq (17)). Together with (15) this is a conditional linear certificate with constant 1/log_2(4/3) and NO connector surcharge.
notes: The constant here (2.4094) is better than S14's cycle constant 2, but it is the ROOT-CONDITIONED statement; S14 (2) proves the stronger target-uniform version over an arbitrary junction basis W containing A.

name: entropy_weighted_short_gap_witness_generalization
statement: (S12 sec.6, scope.) The construction solves a genuine infinite family of three-connected, high-corank cyclic blocks. It does NOT prove the universal linear theorem: the key extra structure is the independent dominating set whose short gaps simultaneously provide (1) one residual direction per three cycle vertices, (2) a full-dual coordinate transversal, and (3) a product activation profile. The remaining global problem is to replace these short-gap witnesses by an entropy-weighted analogue in an ARBITRARY singleton-layer cyclic block.
notes: The three ingredients are separable and are enforced by DIFFERENT checks: (2) by coordinate-basis coverage, (3) by the activation matching. Measured here that (3) alone does not pin the dimension -- so the hard transfer is of ingredients (1)+(2), not of the counting profile.

name: exact_rational_selector_checker_S13
statement: Checker using ONLY integer arithmetic and fractions.Fraction (no floating point). construction(n) builds A = e_0, B_i, C_i, the residuals {A+B_u : u in starts} and the S12 gap-wise basis. structural_check(n) asserts: |starts| = d = (n+2)//3; gaps in {2,3}; |basis| = r = n+1 and rank(basis) = r; |residuals| = d and rank(residuals) = d; and that EVERY form of D_n is 'covered', i.e. there is a basis element b and a sign in {-1,+1} with rank(residuals + [form - sign*b]) = d (the selector residual lies in R). activation_check(n) enumerates all independent sets of C_n, groups them by z = restriction to starts, and asserts count <= 2^{n-d-|z|} and 2*count <= 2^{n+1-d-|z|}. Defaults: structural n = 4..30, activation n = 4..16.
notes: The checker verifies the SPECIFIC construction; it does NOT minimize over all bases/selectors, so it cannot by itself certify that d_cb equals ceil(n/3) rather than merely being at most it. The lower bound is entirely S10's mod-2 argument.

name: s14_cycle_selector_basis_eq14
statement: (S14 (10)-(20).) Put d = ceil(n/3), s = 3d-n in {0,1,2}; choose cyclically ordered U = {u_1,...,u_d} with exactly s gaps of length two and d-s of length three (lengths sum 2s+3(d-s) = n). Write a length-two gap as u_j,m_j,u_{j+1} and a length-three gap as u_j,m_j,w_j,u_{j+1}. Then B_n = {A} u {C_{u_j,m_j} : all j} u (length-three gaps) {C_{m_j,w_j}, B_{w_j}} u (length-two gaps) {B_{m_j}} has 1+d+2(d-s)+s = n+1 forms and is a coordinate basis: relative to A a length-two gap contributes B_{u_j}+B_{m_j}, B_{m_j}, a length-three gap B_{u_j}+B_{m_j}, B_{m_j}+B_{w_j}, B_{w_j}, on disjoint coordinate sets. Selectors: B_{u_j} -> -A (residual L_{u_j}); B_{m_j} -> C_{u_j,m_j} in a length-three gap (residual -L_{u_j}); with v_j = m_j or w_j, C_{v_j,u_{j+1}} -> B_{v_j} (residual L_{u_{j+1}}).
notes: All selector residuals lie in the d-dimensional R = span{L_u}, so d_cb(A_n) <= d, and with S10's lower bound this proves d_cb = d_geo = ceil(n/3).

name: s12_and_s14_selector_bases_differ
statement: S12 and S14 give two DIFFERENT explicit coordinate bases proving the same upper bound d_cb(A_n) <= ceil(n/3). For a gap starting at u with m = u+1, w = u+2: S12 selects {B_m, C_m} (length two) and {B_m, C_m, C_w} (length three); S14 (14) selects {C_u, B_m} (length two) and {C_u, C_m, B_w} (length three). Both are proved to be coordinate bases drawn from the full dual with all selector residuals in span{L_u : u in U}.
source: dossier pp.175-177 (S12 lines 86-142) vs pp.186-189 (S14 lines 122-221)
notes: Verified by this digester (the S13 code implements S12's basis; S14's differs in which C-form of each gap is taken). Useful downstream: the certificate is NOT unique, so a generalization is not forced to reproduce one particular basis -- only the short-gap structure.

name: dcb_table_n4_to_n8
statement: (S14 eq (22).) Exact basis-and-selector enumeration for 4 <= n <= 8 gives d_cb = 2, 2, 2, 3, 3 for n = 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 respectively. The dossier states explicitly: 'The computation is only a check; equations (14)-(21) prove all n.'

name: target_uniform_activation_cell_cycle
statement: (S14 (23)-(26).) Z_u = 1{L_u != 0}; after conditioning on the root sign A this is the occupancy indicator of u in the corresponding stable set. Match every u_j to the FIRST vertex m_j of its following gap; the matched vertices are distinct and lie outside U. Fix an activation pattern z contained in U: the d signs on U are fixed and every active u in z forces its matched neighbour to be unoccupied. Hence, FOR EVERY fixed root value and every additional ancestor boundary value w, |(A_n)_{W=w, Z=z}| <= 2^{n-d-|z|}. Incompatible patterns give an empty cell; exactly, on the full rooted cycle the cell count is the number of independent sets of C_n[V \ (U u N(z))]. Summing, |supp(B_1,...,B_n | W=w)| <= 2^n (3/4)^d.
notes: TARGET-UNIFORM is the operative strengthening over S12 (2): the bound holds for every boundary value w, not just on the root marginal. So (14) is not merely a selector basis but a target-uniform CONDITIONAL activation-cell certificate.

name: cycle_connector_absorption_exact
statement: (S14 (27)-(28).) Let W be an incoming junction basis containing A and otherwise disjoint from the private coordinate span Q = {B_1,...,B_n}. Then R cap span W = 0, because a combination sum_u c_u (A+B_u) lying in the boundary has all private coefficients c_u = 0. Therefore for EVERY ancestor residual space R_< contained in span W: R cap span W is contained in R_<, and dim((R+R_<)/R_<) = d = ceil(n/3). This is the exact connector-absorption condition.
notes: Absorption here is FREE (holds for every R_<, even R_< = 0) because the residual space is entirely private. That is exactly what fails for the m=1 interval, where the residuals are entirely BOUNDARY.

name: rooted_connector_estimate_constant_two
statement: (S14 (2), proved via (28)-(34).) If the common root sign A is the incoming boundary and the n cycle signs are private, the residual space has zero intersection with the boundary and its new rank is at most twice the private conditional defect: dim R = ceil(n/3) <= 2(n - H(B_1,...,B_n | W)) = 2 L_{Q|W}. Hence rooted NAE cycles are connector-compatible cyclic SCCs WITH CONSTANT 2, whenever the only shared cycle coordinate is the homogenizing root (additional disjoint ancestor coordinates are harmless). Ingredients: L_{Q|W} >= n - log_2 L_n because every conditional private support sits inside the independent sets of C_n (31); and ceil(n/3) <= 2(n - log_2 L_n) for all n >= 4 (32).
source: dossier p.184 (S14 lines 21-34), proof pp.190-192 (S14 lines 285-367)
notes: Constant 2 for the cycle. Note the completely uniform (weaker-coefficient) version from the activation cells is d <= L_{Q|W}/log_2(4/3), coefficient 2.4094 (S14 (29)-(30), p.191).

name: disjoint_edge_defect_lower_bound
statement: (S14 (33),(33a),(34).) Choosing floor(n/2) disjoint cycle edges and using their NAE constraints gives n - log_2 L_n >= floor(n/2) * log_2(4/3). With beta = log_2(4/3), for n >= 14 one has 2*beta*floor(n/2) >= beta(n-1) >= (n+2)/3 >= ceil(n/3); the middle inequality holds at n = 14 and thereafter the left side has larger slope because beta > 1/3. The ten remaining values 4 <= n <= 13 follow from (L_4,...,L_13) = (7,11,18,29,47,76,123,199,322,521). This proves ceil(n/3) <= 2(n - log_2 L_n) for all n >= 4.
notes: beta = 0.4150375 > 1/3 is the whole slope argument. Re-verified here for 4 <= n <= 200 (no violations), well beyond the proof's own split at n = 14; the ten small cases were checked individually and all hold.

name: path_selector_distance_theorem_4_1
statement: (S14 Theorem 4.1, eq (36).) For the stable-set fibre of the path P_N (full dual D(P_N) = {A} u {B_i : 0<=i<N} u {C_i = A+B_i+B_{i+1} : 0<=i<N-1}, rank N+1, 2N projective forms), for every N >= 3: d_cb(A_{P_N}) = d_geo(A_{P_N}) = ceil((N-1)/3). Lower bound: the same mod-2 translation gives S(P_N) = {0, u_i} u {u_i+u_{i+1}}, and for a w-dimensional quotient kernel the occupied-coset count is at least 1+(N-w)+max{0, N-1-2w} >= 2N-3w; rationalizing and reducing the saturated lattice transfers this to real signed classes; a feasible quotient has at most N+1 classes, so N+1 >= 2N-3w, i.e. w >= ceil((N-1)/3).
notes: The path is the CUT version of the cycle; it is the object that carries the boundary/connector analysis, since its two ends become incoming boundary.

name: interval_selector_basis_table_41
statement: (S14 (40)-(45).) Write N = m+2 with boundary vertices 0, m+1 and private interval 1,...,m; put d_m = ceil((m+1)/3). Choose an independent U in {1,...,m}, |U| = d_m, so every component of P_{m+2} - U has one or two vertices; one fixed choice: m=1 -> {1}; m=2 -> {2}; m=3 -> {1,3}; m=3k (k>=2) -> {2,4} u {7,10,...,3k-2} u {3k} (middle progression empty at k=2); m=3k+1 -> {2,5,...,3k-1} u {3k+1}; m=3k+2 -> {2,5,...,3k+2}. Every two-vertex component {v,w} is immediately followed by a distinct selected u in U; use B_v, C_{v,w}, C_{w,u}; for a one-vertex component {v} use B_v; also use A; finally add B_u for every selected u not occurring in such a block. Take R_m = span{A+B_u : u in U}.
notes: Coordinate-basis proof: relative to A a block is triangular on B_v, B_v+B_w, B_w+B_u and distinct blocks use disjoint selected vertices. Crucially the first and last component representatives are B_0 and B_{m+1}, so {A, B_0, B_{m+1}} is contained in the basis (eq (44)) -- this is what makes the certificate boundary-preserving. Table sizes and independence re-verified here for m = 1..7.

name: boundary_preserving_interval_certificate
statement: (S14 (46)-(48), eq (3).) Regard W = {A, B_0, B_{m+1}} as the incoming boundary and Q = {B_1,...,B_m} as the private junction basis. Eq (44) shows the selector basis preserves every incoming coordinate; since all u in U are private, R_m cap span W = 0. Hence for any previously paid R_< contained in span W: dim((R_m+R_<)/R_<) = d_m = ceil((m+1)/3) and R_m cap span W is contained in R_<. The basis and selectors do NOT depend on the values of the boundary signs, so they survive the genuinely affine conditional fibres created by fixing W.
notes: Boundary-value independence is the property that makes this usable inside a recursive/conditional argument; a certificate that depended on w would not survive conditioning.

name: interval_conditional_entropy_bound
statement: (S14 (49).) For any law supported on the interval constraints, fixing W = w leaves a subset of the independent sets of a path on m vertices. Hence H(Q | W=w) <= log_2 F_{m+2} and L_{Q|W} := m - H(Q|W) >= m - log_2 F_{m+2}.
notes: F_{m+2} is the number of independent sets of P_m. This is the entropy-only route, which is what survives at m = 3 where the sharper cellwise route provably fails.

name: interval_linear_bound_C_int
statement: (S14 eq (4).) For every m >= 2, d_m <= C_int * (m - H(Q|W)) with C_int = 2/(3 - log_2 5) = 2.949539... . Proof: with beta = log_2(4/3), m=2 gives L_{Q|W} >= 2-log_2 3 = beta while d_m = 1; m=3 gives L_{Q|W} >= 3-log_2 5 with d_m = 2, which is EXACTLY the claimed inequality; for m >= 4, floor(m/2) disjoint private edges give L_{Q|W} >= beta*floor(m/2), and C_int*beta > 6/5 follows from (4/3)^5 > (8/5)^3 i.e. 128000 > 124416, so m = 4,5 are immediate and for m >= 6, C_int*beta*floor(m/2) > (6/5)(m-1)/2 = 3(m-1)/5 >= (m+3)/3 >= ceil((m+1)/3).
notes: m = 3 is the tight case (equality by construction), which is why C_int is what it is. The chain 3(m-1)/5 >= (m+3)/3 requires exactly m >= 6, and the integer certificate 128000 > 124416 is exact. All steps re-verified numerically here.

name: C_int_optimality_limit
statement: (S14 (56).) The coefficient C_int = 2/(3-log_2 5) = 2.949539... is OPTIMAL for a theorem uniform over arbitrary descendant attachments. Witness: at m = 3 attach k later stable-set vertices, each adjacent to both boundary endpoints and to no private interval vertex. When both endpoints are unoccupied those later vertices are free and the five private independent sets of P_3 occur with equal multiplicity 2^k; other boundary patterns have only O(1) extensions. As k -> infinity, H(Q|W) -> log_2 5 and d_m/L_{Q|W} -> 2/(3-log_2 5) = C_int.
notes: IMPORTANT FOR THE CAMPAIGN'S CONSTANT FLOOR: within pp.156-200 this 2.9495 is the largest forced constant, exceeding the 1/log_2(4/3) = 2.40942 floor cited from S6 p.113. Any theorem uniform over descendant attachments must tolerate C >= 2.9495 on intervals. Re-derived here numerically: d_m/L -> 2.949539695 (12 digits at k = 40).

name: target_uniform_interval_cells_m2_and_m_ge_4
statement: (S14 (57)-(60).) Except at m = 1 and m = 3, the choice (41) has a matching entirely INSIDE the private interval, u |-> u-1 for u in U. Define Z_u = 1{A+B_u != 0}. For fixed boundary target w and activation pattern z, the d_m private signs on U are fixed and every active u forces its distinct matched private neighbour to be unoccupied, so |Q_{w,z}| <= 2^{m-d_m-|z|} for m = 2 or m >= 4. This is target-uniform in BOTH endpoint signs. Summing gives d_m <= L_{Q|W}/log_2(4/3), coefficient 1/log_2(4/3) < 2.410.
notes: The exception set {1,3} is exactly where u-1 leaves the private interval (U contains 1, so u-1 = 0 is a BOUNDARY vertex) -- verified here against the table (41) for m = 1..7. So the m=1 and m=3 pathologies have the same syntactic cause even though their consequences differ.

name: m3_interval_cellwise_certificate_impossible
statement: (S14 (61)-(62).) At m = 3 the neutral boundary fibre is the five independent sets of P_3. A dimension-two private CELLWISE certificate would imply 5 <= 2^3 (3/4)^2 = 9/2, which is impossible. Concretely, for the residuals U = {1,3} the all-active cell consists of exactly ONE point whereas its putative bound is 2^{3-2-2} = 1/2. Hence the entropy-only estimate, rather than the sharp activation profile, is genuinely necessary for this finite affine interval.
notes: CONDITION OF FAILURE: m = 3 only. Re-verified exactly here by enumeration: at m = 3 exactly one cell violates (z = (1,1), count 1 > 1/2) and the aggregate 5 <= 4.5 fails; at m = 2,4,5,6,7 there are ZERO violations. This is the falsifier that gives the whole activation machinery teeth.

name: m1_interval_no_absolute_constant_defect_bound
statement: (S14 sec.7, (63)-(64).) The one-private-vertex interval (boundary 0,2, private 1) admits NO defect-only connector bound with an absolute constant. For the neutral boundary state both signs of B_1 occur, so its private defect is zero -- and this can dominate a SPANNING, FULL-CLOSED fibre, not merely an isolated nonspanning boundary state. Attach k further stable-set vertices z_1,...,z_k each adjacent to both boundary vertices 0,2 and to nothing else: in the positive half the neutral endpoint pattern has 2^{k+1} extensions (B_1 and all z_j free), each other endpoint pattern has one. Then H(B_1|A,B_0,B_2) = 2^{k+1}/(2^{k+1}+3) and L_{Q|W} = 3/(2^{k+1}+3) -> 0, while the local path has exact selector distance ONE. So no inequality dim((R+R_<)/R_<) <= C * L_{Q|W} can hold with an absolute C.
notes: THE decisive obstruction in this source range: it is why the connector-absorption clause is a HYPOTHESIS of the open target rather than a convenience. Quantifier detail: the failure is for R_< = 0 (no prepaid boundary residual); with the two boundary residuals prepaid the block is free. Re-derived here exactly for k = 0..7: L = 3/(2^{k+1}+3) matches for every k.

name: m1_exact_absorbed_alternative
statement: (S14 (65)-(67).) The same m=1 block has an exact ABSORBED alternative: use the coordinate basis {A,B_0,B_1,B_2} and assign both edge forms to B_1, giving C_{0,1} - B_1 = A+B_0 and C_{1,2} - B_1 = A+B_2. Both residuals lie entirely in the boundary. If span{A+B_0, A+B_2} is contained in R_<, the block costs ZERO new rank and satisfies connector absorption. If they have not been paid, these residuals violate the absorption condition and one must use the private residual A+B_1, at new cost one. The block is acyclic and belongs in the triangular/ancestor-absorption part of a recursive proof, not in a defect-only cyclic-core theorem.
notes: This is the exact statement behind the campaign's two-regime reading: defect-poor blocks are not uncharted, they have KNOWN zero-cost certificates CONDITIONAL on ancestor payment. The dichotomy (zero new rank if prepaid, cost one if not) is exact, not asymptotic.

name: treat_m1_interval_as_independent_cyclic_core
statement: FAILS. Treating a one-private-vertex interval as an independent cyclic core would repeat precisely the connector direction which condition (14) of `recursive_paired_block_tree_entropy.md` was designed to absorb. Such a block cannot be charged locally by conditional defect; it must either pass its boundary residuals to an ancestor or be handled by the global triangular activation budget.
notes: CONDITION OF FAILURE: acyclic defect-poor blocks with all residuals in the boundary and no ancestor payment. The named external condition (14) is in a file the campaign has established does not exist on any machine we control -- see recursive_paired_block_tree_entropy_condition_14.

name: recursive_paired_block_tree_entropy_condition_14
statement: S14 sec.8 names condition (14) of `recursive_paired_block_tree_entropy.md` as the clause designed to ABSORB the connector direction that a one-private-vertex interval would otherwise repeat. That is the identification of the external telescope file's condition (14) with the connector-absorption condition R cap span W contained in R_<. The file itself is cited but NOT reproduced anywhere in the dossier.

name: s14_section8_three_phenomena_separation
statement: (S14 sec.8.) Three phenomena separated cleanly. (a) A closed rooted NAE cycle with the homogenizer in the boundary is genuinely cyclic and CONNECTOR-COMPATIBLE: selector rank ceil(n/3), residual space with no boundary intersection, conditional defect paying that rank with coefficient 2. (b) Cutting the cycle to an interval preserves an exact boundary-containing selector basis; every interval with at least two private vertices has a uniform conditional linear bound, and all but the three-vertex one have the stronger activation-cell certificate. (c) A one-private-vertex interval cannot be charged locally by conditional defect; it must pass its boundary residuals to an ancestor or be handled by the global triangular activation budget.
notes: S14's own conclusion from (a)-(c): 'rooted NAE cycles themselves are not an obstruction to the desired connector theorem. Their only boundary pathology occurs after cutting them into an acyclic one-vertex interval, and that pathology is exactly resolved by ancestor residual absorption rather than by a new cyclic estimate.' || READING WARNING: this is a statement about the rooted-NAE family, NOT about the residual class.
